SUBJECT: Coal Situation.

The coal situation in Shanghai can be summed up briefly as being extremely critical. As a result of the present Far Eastern Hostilities supplies from North China, Japan and Indo-China have completely stopped. A few days prior to the present hostilities two vessels, chartered by Hongay Sales Co., arrived in port. They were the Portuguese Registered Pluto and the Panamanian Registered Romona. The former carried 5,000 tons of dust and the latter 4,500 tons of anthracite lump coal. It is understood that Hongay Sales are able to unload the Pluto but the Romona and its coal has been seized by the Japanese authorities.

The majority of coal stocks in Shanghai are on wharves situated in Pootung and include most of the stocks owned by the Kailan Mining Administration and other British importers. If the Japanese authorities release these stocks the situation will be alleviated to some extent but in any case there will be practically no coal in Shanghai within a few months if supplies cannot reach this port.

Dealers have been notified that they must reduce their supplies to consumers by 50% and consumers have been requested to reduce their consumption accordingly.

All industrial enterprises have been notified that they must register their stocks and normal consumption. Private individuals have been notified that all stocks of 5 tons and over must be registered

主题：煤炭情况。

上海的煤炭情况可简要概括为极其严峻。由于目前的远东战事，来自华北、日本和印度支那的供应已完全中断。在目前战事爆发前几天，由恒益洋行（Hongay Sales Co.）租用的两艘船只抵达港口。它们是葡萄牙注册的“普鲁托”号（Pluto）和巴拿马注册的“罗莫纳”号（Romona）。前者装载了5,000吨煤粉，后者装载了4,500吨无烟块煤。据悉，恒益洋行能够卸载“普鲁托”号，但“罗莫纳”号及其所载煤炭已被日本当局扣押。

上海的大部分煤炭库存位于浦东的码头，其中包括开滦矿务总局（Kailan Mining Administration）和其他英国进口商拥有的大部分库存。如果日本当局释放这些库存，局势将在一定程度上得到缓解，但无论如何，如果供应无法抵达本港，几个月内上海实际上将无煤可用。

December 14, 1941.

Coal Situation.

The coal situation in Shanghai can be summed
up briefly as being extremely critical. As a result
of the present Far Eastern Hostilities supplies from
North China, Japan and Indo-China have completely
stopped. A few days prior to the present hostilities
two vessels, chartered by Hongay Sales Co., arrived
in port. They were the Portuguese Registered Pluto
and the Panamenian Registered Romona. The former
carried 5,000 tons of dust and the latter 4,500 tons
of anthracite lump coal. It is understood that
Hongay Sales are able to unload the Pluto but the
Romona and its coal has been seized by the Japanese
authorities.

The majority of coal stocks in Shanghai are
on wharves situated in Pootung and include most of
the stocks owned by the Kailan Mining Administration
and other British importers. If the Japanese
authorities release these stocks the situation will
be alleviated to some extent but in any case there will
be practically no coal in Shanghai within a few
months if supplies cannot reach this port.

Dealers have been notified that they must
reduce their supplies to consumers by 50% and consumers
have been requested to reduce their consumption
accordingly.

All industrial enterprises have been notified
that they must register their stocks and normal
consumption. Private individuals have been notified
that all stocks of 5 tons and over must be registered

No. S. U. C.
REPORT

S.I. Special Branch Sta 467. File No.................... Date December 9, 1941.

SUBJECT: Coal Situation

During the month of November an average tonnage
of coal arrived in Shanghai and with the promise of
official exchange by the Stabilization Board it
appeared that the coal situation would be greatly
ameliorated.

The outbreak of war between Japan and the
U.S.A. and Great Britain has changed the whole situation.
It has been thought that coal could be brought to
Shanghai in boats of Panamanian registry but it was
noticed on December 9th, 1941, that a vessel of that
flag, The Romona, chartered by Hongay Sales Ltd., was
being unloaded by the Japanese. This vessel is lying
at Nos. 1 and 2 buoys and had about 4,500 tons of lump
anthracite in the holds. 1,200 tons had been
removed by Hongay Sales when Japan declared war and
since then the Japanese have taken over the boat.

Another Hongay chartered vessel, The Pluto
(Portuguese registered) is lying at 21 and 22 buoys
but there is no information available as to what has
happened to it or the 5,000 tons of anthracite in the
holds.

The whole situation is extremely obscure except
for the fact that coal stocks are very low and there
is at present no way of them being replenished.

主题：煤炭情况

11月份期间，平均吨位的煤炭运抵上海，随着平准会承诺提供官方汇率，煤炭情况似乎将大大改善。

日本与美国及英国之间战争的爆发改变了整个局势。人们曾认为煤炭可以通过巴拿马注册的船只运至上海，但在1941年12月9日注意到，一艘悬挂该国旗、由恒益有限公司（Hongay Sales Ltd.）租用的船只“罗莫纳”号（The Romona）正由日本人卸货。该船停泊在第1和第2号浮筒处，舱内约有4,500吨无烟块煤。在日本宣战时，恒益洋行已卸下1,200吨，此后日本人接管了该船。

除了煤炭库存非常低且目前无法补充这一事实外，整个局势极其不明朗。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
No. B. D.
S. 1, Special Branch /Station. File No.................... Date....November 10, 1941..

SUBJECT: Coal Situation.

The coal situation during the month of October
1941 was even more serious than in previous months.
Prices have again soared to hitherto unthought of figures
and are even higher now than those quoted at the end
of October.

If the Council's representatives are successful
in obtaining foreign exchange to cover coal imports,
a decided drop in prices is forecast. Official
exchange is not only required to cover the actual
cost of coal but also for the extremely high freight
charges which are more than double the cost of the
coal itself. For example importers must pay G.$5.00
per ton for anthracite in Indo-China but freight
charges to Shanghai are approximately G$11.00 per ton.

Messrs. Hongay Sales are believed unable to
obtain ships in which to bring their December supplies
to Shanghai due to the fact that shipping companies
are demanding payment in gold dollars. Should the
stabilization board grant foreign exchange to local
coal importers before their present gold reserves are
exhausted, the above predicament will be greatly eased.
Present stocks of anthracite plus November supplies
en route are not expected to last beyond the middle
of December.

As a consequence of the existing shortage
it is understood that Hongay Sales have been forced
to cease supplying anthracite nuts to some 300
laundries, dry cleaners, foundries and barber shops.

编号 B. D.
S. 1, 特别科 /警署。档案号.................... 日期....1941年11月10日..

主题：煤炭形势。

1941年10月期间的煤炭形势比前几个月更为严峻。
价格再次飙升至此前难以想象的水平，
甚至高于10月底的报价。

如果工部局代表能够成功获得用于支付煤炭进口的外汇，
预计价格将显著下降。官方汇率不仅需覆盖煤炭的实际
成本，还需支付极高的运费，后者是煤炭本身成本的两倍多。例如，进口商必须为法属印度支那的无烟煤支付每吨国币$5.00，但运至上海的运费约为每吨国币$11.00。

据信，由于航运公司要求以金美元支付，鸿基销售公司（Messrs. Hongay Sales）无法租到船只将其12月份的供应物资运抵上海。如果平准基金委员会在当地煤炭进口商目前的黄金储备耗尽之前向其提供外汇，上述困境将大大缓解。目前的无烟煤库存加上途中的11月份供应物资，预计维持不到12月中旬。

由于现有的短缺，据悉鸿基销售公司已被迫停止向约300家洗衣店、干洗店、铸造厂和理发店供应无烟煤粒煤。

SUBJECT: Coal Situation

Tea house coal prices quoted at the end of September reveal a further slight increase in the price of bituminous coals but a decrease is noted in anthracite prices. During the month of September arrivals of bituminous coal totalled 164,640 tons, an increase of 35,630 tons compared with the August figures. A large drop is noted in the arrivals of anthracite coal, only 34,900 tons being registered compared with the 67,200 tons imported in August. Very little anthracite arrived in Shanghai from Hopei or Korea during the month. Supplies from Hongay and Haiphong, however, are normal at present.

It is reliably learned that an application by Messrs. Hongay Sales to the Currency Stabilization Board for exchange has been refused and that as a consequence the price of anthracite coal will be increased about $20 per ton within a few days and in all probability further increases of $30 per ton are foreseen. These increases are unavoidable and are the result of the Hongay Company having to purchase gold in the "Black Market" in consequence of the Stabilization Board's decision. It will be realized that as all payments for coal in Indo-China have to be made in gold, Hongay Sales must obtain gold exchange at whatever exchange is available.

Coal Situation

Except for considerable increases in prices
there has been no marked change in the coal situation
during the month of August. The high prices now
prevailing are attributed to the refusal by Japanese
Authorities to release any appreciable quantities
of coal from the huge stocks which they control.
129,010 tons of bituminous coal arrived in
Shanghai during the month. This shows a decrease
of approximately 33,000 tons compared with July's
figures. An increase of approximately 4,000 tons
of anthracite coal arrived in port during the month.
A comparison of the July and August total arrivals
of all coal show a decrease of about 30,000 tons.
Stocks on wharves, however, have increased
by about 11,000 tons. In view of the fact that the
demand for coal has not declined in any way it
must be assumed that certain quarters are continuing
the hoarding of this commodity. It is a matter of
conjecture whether the reason for this hoarding is
one of possible future financial gain or of military
necessity.
It is reliably learned that ship freight
charges on coal from the South have been reduced
by about G.$1.00 during the past two months. This
would, no doubt, have a marked effect on coal prices
if it were possible to effect the release of the
stocks mentioned in the preceding paragraph.
It is again necessary to draw attention to

煤炭形势

除了价格大幅上涨外，8月份煤炭形势没有明显变化。
目前的高价归因于日本当局拒绝从其控制的巨大库存中释放任何可观数量的煤炭。
本月有129,010吨烟煤运抵上海。与7月份的数据相比，这显示减少了约33,000吨。本月港口无烟煤到货量增加了约4,000吨。比较7月和8月所有煤炭的总到货量，显示减少了约30,000吨。
然而，码头库存增加了约11,000吨。鉴于对煤炭的需求并未以任何方式减少，必须假定某些方面正在继续囤积这种商品。这种囤积的原因是出于未来可能的经济利益还是军事需要，纯属猜测。
据可靠消息获悉，过去两个月来自南方的煤炭船运费已降低约国币$1.00。如果能够释放前一段提到的库存，这无疑会对煤炭价格产生显著影响。

S.1, 特别支部站/ 档案号 日期 1941年9月10日。

主题：煤炭局势

除价格大幅上涨外，8月份煤炭局势没有明显变化。目前的高价归因于日本当局拒绝从其控制的巨大库存中释放任何可观数量的煤炭。

本月抵达上海的烟煤为129,010吨。与7月份的数据相比，这显示减少了约33,000吨。本月抵港的无烟煤增加了约4,000吨。比较7月和8月所有煤炭的总到货量，显示减少了约30,000吨。

然而，码头库存增加了约11,000吨。鉴于对煤炭的需求丝毫没有下降，必须假定某些方面正在继续囤积这种商品。这种囤积是出于未来可能的经济利益还是军事需要，纯属猜测。

据可靠消息，过去两个月来自南方的煤炭船运费已降低约国币$1.00。如果能够释放前一段提到的库存，这无疑会对煤炭价格产生显著影响。

再次有必要提请注意

S.1, Special Branch,
August 10, 1941.

Coal Situation

Since the last report on this subject the
situation has undergone changes which do not
reveal a very encouraging state of affairs.
The main factor contributing to the
unsatisfactory situation is still the difficulty
in obtaining the necessary shipping facilities.
The high freight charges obtaining on those ships
which are available is the largest contributory
cause for the existing abnormal prices.
Although coal arrivals during July have
registered a further drop it is noted that stocks
on wharves have increased approximately 50,000 tons
above the June figures. These wharves are all under
Japanese control.
A further rise in prices was recorded at the
end of July, due to further increases in freight
charges.
It is apparent that local dealers are
experiencing increasing difficulty in obtaining
sufficient stocks of soft coal for household
purposes. It has been learned that the Nyi Tai
Shing and other Companies, unable to obtain sufficient
supplies from their usual source, recently made
application to the Japanese authorities for the
release of part of the huge stocks of soft coal
lying at the Pootung Wharves. The Japanese Authorities
promised to release 30,000 tons to these dealers,
and although this figure was far below the actual
pages.zh:
S.1, 特别支部，
1941年8月10日。

煤炭局势

自上次关于此主题的报告以来，局势发生了一些变化，显示出并不令人鼓舞的状态。造成这种不满意局势的主要因素仍然是难以获得必要的航运设施。现有船只的高昂运费是导致目前异常价格的最大原因。

尽管7月份的煤炭到货量进一步下降，但注意到码头库存比6月份的数据增加了约50,000吨。这些码头均处于日本控制之下。

由于运费进一步上涨，7月底记录到价格再次上涨。

显然，本地经销商在获取足够的家用软煤库存方面正面临越来越大的困难。据悉，义泰兴 (Nyi Tai Shing) 及其他公司因无法从通常来源获得足够供应，最近向日本当局申请释放存放在浦东码头的部分巨大软煤库存。日本当局承诺向这些经销商释放30,000吨，尽管这一数字远低于实际

pages.en:
- 2 -
requirements, it was nevertheless sufficient to
temporarily alleviate the situation. The promised
30,000 tons, however, did not materialize and the
dealers have now received information that the
Japanese Authorities were only prepared to allow
the release of 4,000 tons. This figure is obviously
inadequate and the situation resulting from this
state of affairs is one of extreme precariousness.
When it is remembered that the present summer demand
for soft coal falls far below the coming winter needs,
it will be readily realized that future prospects
present a very gloomy outlook unless a successful
solution is found immediately.
With reference to the report of the Coal
Sub-Committee's Meeting held on July 17th, 1941,
and Mr. Hutton's remarks re the possibility of the
Police obtaining figures of coal arrivals from the
Customs, I have to report that the Customs absolutely
refuse to give any information of this nature. All
enquiries are referred to the Customs Report which
is on sale at Messrs. Kelly & Walsh on the 22nd of
each month. This Report gives statistics on coal
shipments for the preceding month. It will be
appreciated that the Police Report on the Coal
Situation is forwarded to the S.M.C. by the 10th
of each month.
The statement in the Coal Sub-Committee's
Report that Police figures do not include Pootung
stocks is obviously inaccurate when it is remembered
pages.zh:

需求，但仍足以暂时缓解局势。然而，承诺的30,000吨并未兑现，经销商现在收到的消息是，日本当局只准备允许释放4,000吨。这个数字显然不足，由此产生的局势极其岌岌可危。

考虑到目前夏季对软煤的需求远低于即将到来的冬季需求，人们很容易意识到，除非立即找到成功的解决方案，否则未来的前景非常黯淡。

关于1941年7月17日举行的煤炭小组委员会会议报告，以及 Hutton 先生关于警方是否可能从海关获得煤炭到货数据的评论，我必须报告说，海关绝对拒绝提供此类信息。所有查询均被指引至每月22日在凯利·沃尔什公司 (Messrs. Kelly & Walsh) 出售的《海关报告》。该报告提供上个月的煤炭运输统计数据。应当理解，警方关于煤炭局势的报告是在每月10日之前发送给上海公共租界工部局 (S.M.C.) 的。

煤炭小组委员会报告中称警方数据不包括浦东库存的说法，显然不准确，因为记得

In March 1940, the S.M.C. went into the
possibility of adopting measures to limit the prices
of coal in the Settlement. A Kailan Mining Administration
official commenting on this stated that it is impossible
to control selling prices while there is a shortage of
coal. He also pointed out that there is a law of
supply and demand and in certain trades, shipping in
particular, the whole basis of price fixing is what
the charterer will pay.

Sir Robert Calder Marshall in reviewing the
above stated that he could not see how the Council,
under the conditions existing then, would be able to
control prices effectively, for the factors which
control price are market demand and replacement cost,
and unless a greater supply of coal becomes available
it would appear inevitable that prices would remain
at replacing cost.

Imports

The amount of coal arriving in Shanghai
during the month of March 1940, when the above views
were expressed, was 247,000 tons. By March 1941, the
imports had dropped to 146,000 tons and in April 1941
the figure was even lower, i.e. 100,600 tons.

The average monthly tonnage from all sources
arriving in Shanghai for the past twelve months was 170,000.

Consumption

The normal monthly consumption of coal in
Shanghai a year ago was approximately 200,000 tons.
This included the Shanghai Power Company's consumption
of 40,000 to 50,000 tons per month.

Owing to various factors, the chief of which
is the Japanese blockade of China ports, which prevented

1940年3月，工部局曾探讨采取措施限制租界内煤炭价格的可能性。一位开滦矿务局官员对此评论称，在煤炭短缺的情况下，不可能控制销售价格。他还指出，存在供求规律，在某些行业，特别是航运业，定价的全部基础在于承租人的支付意愿。

罗伯特·考尔德·马歇尔爵士在审查上述内容时表示，他看不出在当时存在的条件下，公董局如何能有效控制价格，因为控制价格的因素是市场需求和重置成本，除非有更多的煤炭供应，否则价格似乎不可避免地会维持在重置成本水平。

进口

在上述观点发表时，即1940年3月，抵达上海的煤炭数量为247,000吨。到1941年3月，进口量已降至146,000吨，而1941年4月的数字甚至更低，即100,600吨。

过去十二个月从所有来源抵达上海的月平均吨位为170,000吨。

消费

一年前，上海的正常月煤炭消费量约为200,000吨。其中包括上海电力公司每月40,000至50,000吨的消费量。

factories from obtaining the necessary raw materials
from the interior and thus forcing them to curtail their
operations, the monthly local consumption of coal has
dropped considerably. The added drop in the demand
for bunker coal, caused by the curtailment of shipping
services to Shanghai, has brought the monthly
consumption down to an estimated 150,000 - 180,000
tons or even lower.

The cause of the gradual increase in local
stocks (from approximately 181,000 tons in April 1940
to approximately 243,300 tons in April 1941) is the
accumulating of supplies by Japanese concerns notably
the M.B.K. It will be seen from the table attached
that a large percentage of coal imported from Japanese
sources has been for the M.B.K. What happens to this
coal after arrival at M.B.K. wharves, is, of course, not
known, but information, which incidentally is confirmed
by the increasing stock figures, is that this coal is being
accumulated by this concern (M.B.K.). As was mentioned
in the report of April 1940, this coal is no doubt of an
inferior quality, as a reported shortage of coal in
Japan at that time would seem to indicate that there
would not be any good quality coal available for export
to China.

Now, it would appear that these large stocks
of coal held by Japanese, may be offered for sale on
the local market at a fixed price, which would no
doubt be in excess of the actual value of the coal concerned.

The present high prices prevailing in Shanghai
pages.zh:
- 2 -

工厂从内地获取必要的原材料，从而迫使它们缩减运营，本地月煤炭消费量已大幅下降。加上由于往返上海的航运服务缩减导致船用燃料煤需求进一步下降，月消费量已降至估计的150,000 - 180,000吨，甚至更低。

本地库存逐渐增加的原因（从1940年4月的约181,000吨增加到1941年4月的约243,300吨）是日本企业，特别是南满铁道株式会社（M.B.K.）在积累供应。从附表中可以看出，从日本来源进口的煤炭中有很大比例是供给南满铁道株式会社的。这些煤炭抵达南满铁道株式会社码头后的去向，当然无人知晓，但据信（这一信息也得到库存数字增加的佐证），该机构（南满铁道株式会社）正在囤积这些煤炭。正如1940年4月的报告中所述，这些煤炭的质量无疑较差，因为当时据报道日本国内煤炭短缺，这似乎表明没有优质煤炭可供出口到中国。

现在，日本人持有的这些大量煤炭库存，似乎可能会以固定价格在本地市场出售，该价格无疑会超过相关煤炭的实际价值。

Whilst the foregoing is merely a

T. Robertson, Esq.
May 9, 1941.

COAL SITUATION

The coal situation at the end of April is
in effect not greatly changed from that prevailing
at the end of the previous month.

The expected drop in the import of anthracite
coal has manifested itself, as will be noticed by the
figure of 18,300 tons imported from Hongay and Haiphong
during April as against 54,800 tons during March. The
freight charges have been considerably increased and are
now as high as U.S.$15 and $17 per ton. A further increase
is foreseen.

As the bulk of coal briquettes consists of
anthracite coal, it will be realized that a shortage
of briquettes will be felt unless a solution of the
shipping problem is found.

It was reported in the Shanghai Times of May 1,
that quantities of coal were being imported from the
Mentoukou mines, near Peking. If these extra supplies
are actually imported into Shanghai and made available to
small consumers, it may be possible for this coal to be
used in the place of briquettes.

However it is learned that the average daily
output of the Mentoukou mines is as low as approximately
500 tons. It is fairly obvious that the figure of
50,000 tons mentioned in the newspaper report will
cover a long period, as out of a daily output of
500 tons, it will not be possible to reserve large
quantities for Shanghai after the normal demands have
been met.

With regard to profiteering, it is possible
that some dealers who have had stocks on hand for some
time are endeavouring to obtain a higher price for
this coal than usual, but, as mentioned in a
previous report, the cost of replacement which is
increasing monthly, must be met. Measures have been
adopted by importers to curb the activities of
profiteers by ascertaining the reason for large
purchases by other than their usual customers. Unless
it is proved that the demand is genuine stocks are
not released to these applicants. It is reported that
with the freight charges continually increasing, the
present high prices do not allow an excessive margin of
profit.

The stocks of coal held by Japanese interests,
mentioned in the March report, are gradually increasing
but are still not available for general consumption.

煤炭情况

4月底的煤炭情况实际上与上月末的情况相比变化不大。

预计无烟煤进口量的下降已经显现，从4月从鸿基和海防进口的18,300吨与3月的54,800吨相比即可看出。运费已大幅增加，现在高达每吨15美元和17美元。预计还会进一步上涨。

由于煤球主要由无烟煤组成，可以意识到，除非找到解决航运问题的办法，否则将会感到煤球短缺。

据5月1日的《字林西报》报道，有大批煤炭正从北京附近的门头沟煤矿进口。如果这些额外供应确实进口到上海并提供给小消费者，那么这种煤炭有可能被用来替代煤球。

然而，据悉门头沟煤矿的日均产量低至约500吨。很明显，报纸报道中提到的50,000吨将涵盖很长一段时间，因为在每日500吨的产量中，在满足正常需求后，不可能为上海预留大量煤炭。

关于牟取暴利，有些持有库存一段时间的经销商可能试图以高于平常的价格出售这些煤炭，但是，如前一份报告所述，必须应对每月都在增加的重置成本。进口商已采取措施，通过查明非通常客户进行大量采购的原因来遏制投机者的活动。除非证明需求是真实的，否则不会向这些申请人释放库存。据报道，随着运费不断上涨，目前的高价不允许有过高的利润空间。

3月份报告中提到的由日本利益集团持有的煤炭库存正在逐渐增加，但仍不供一般消费使用。

Fifty Thousand Tons To

A measure of relief for Shang-
hai's coal crisis was promised yes-
terday with the announcement
that the local firm of Messrs.
George McBain have reached an
agreement with the Japanese
authorities to bring 50,000 tons of
coal to Shanghai from the Mentou-
kou mines near Peking.
While, since this coal is of the
anthracite variety, it will not help
the Shanghai Power Company, it
is nevertheless expected to ease
the shortage of coal in this city
for domestic and industrial use. It
is expected that shipments through
this source may be continued.
An official of the firm said that
the first shipments had already
been arranged for, and would be
made early in May. The haul will
be by water.

Will Help Out

While the real need in Shanghai
is for bituminous coal, which con-
stitutes 80 per cent. of the total
monthly consumption of 170,000
tons in this city, this added sup-
ply will help, especially for domes-
tic use, while a few industrial
plants are also equipped to use
anthracite.
As a consequence of the contract,
the stock of the Shanghai Explora-
tion and Development Co., which
manages Mentoukou, rose to $25.50
on the local Stock Exchange. The
stock opened at $23, and a fort-
night ago could be had at $19. The
nominal value is Taels 2.50.

COAL SITUATION
APR 19 1941
SPECIAL

When reviewing the coal situation at the present
time, it is noteworthy that during the month of March, no
arrivals of Indian coal are recorded. The total imports of
bituminous coals, however, do not show a large decrease over
the February figures. That this is so is due to the fact that
additional ships have recently been obtained to transport coal
from North China and fairly large stocks of bituminous coal are
on hand at the present time. Incidentally, large quantities of
coal are being accumulated by certain Japanese (presumably
military) interests, but are not being released for general
consumption, large Japanese concerns allegedly being unable to
obtain supplies of this coal.

It is once again necessary to draw attention to
articles in the local press concerning the coal market. On
April 7, an article appeared in the North China Daily News
referring to the activities of speculators on the coal market.
Whilst it is true that prices are continually increasing, the
view is expressed by importers that reports of large-
scale profiteering are not strictly correct. These reports
probably owe their origination to the fact that certain small
dealers have been compelled to increase their prices, to be
able to cover the increased cost of replacement stocks. In
addition, large consumers such as the utility companies, are
reported to be purchasing large stocks locally, owing to the
impossibility of obtaining Indian coal and no doubt the prices
that they are prepared to pay rise in proportion to the urgency
of the demand.

To say that the hoarding of stocks is chiefly
responsible for the present high prices, however, would appear
somewhat exaggerated. It will be remembered that mention was
made in the report dated March 10, that the efforts of some
dealers to obtain reserve stocks had been defeated by importers
having exercised some modicum of control over their distribution.

再次有必要提请人们注意本地报刊上有关煤炭市场的文章。4月7日，《字林西报》刊登了一篇文章，提及煤炭市场上的投机活动。虽然价格确实在不断上涨，但进口商认为，关于大规模牟取暴利的报道并不完全准确。这些报道的产生可能是因为某些小经销商被迫提高价格，以便能够弥补增加库存补货的成本。此外，据报道，公用事业公司等大型消费者正在本地大量采购库存，这是由于无法获得印度煤炭，而且毫无疑问，他们愿意支付的价格随着需求的紧迫程度而成比例上升。

然而，如果说囤积库存是目前高价的主要原因，似乎有些夸大其词。应该记得，在3月10日的报告中曾提到，一些经销商试图获取储备库存的努力未能成功，因为进口商对其分销行使了一定程度的控制。

Coal Balls Reach
Record Price
Speculators Blamed ; Ample
Stocks of Materials Said
Available in Shanghai

A serious threat to every Chinese
household in Shanghai is the ever-in-
creasing price of coal balls needed
for cooking. The new record price
is $265 per ton. Chinese circles fear
that unless speculation on this im-
portant commodity and daily neces-
sary is stopped, the price may reach
the highest mark of $15 per picul.
Before the war the price was less
than $1 per picul. Besides worrying
about their daily quota of rice, the
poor are searching for fire-wood in
all streets, where hawkers are often
seen selling what appear to be brok-
en parts of coffins chopped into
small pieces.
It is generally agreed among the
Chinese here that, like the rice situa-
tion, the seriousness of the coal ball
situation has also reached a climax
and it is alleged by the Chinese
press that speculators are very active
in the coal market, while the auth-
orities are seeking a remedy for im-
proving the rice situation. Their
purchasing activities and the alleged
hoarding indulged in by coal mer-
chants are said to be chiefly respon-
sible for the increase of prices. In
the face of strong criticisms from
all Chinese quarters, the Machine-
made Coal Ball Merchants Association
is planning to hold a meeting to dis-
cuss the situation.
It is learned, however, that like
the price of rice, the price of coal
is also affected seriously by freight
charges and the increased cost for
maintaining workers by the various
coal ball manufacturing factories.
The reduction of freight charges is
again a very important factor in set-
tling this problem. The material
needed for making coal balls is ar-
riving continuously and the ready
stock amounts to more than 30,000
tons, enough for one month's con-
sumption. About 1,000 tons are sold
daily here.
pages.zh:
煤球价格
创历史新高
归咎于投机者；据称
上海材料库存充足

上海每个中国家庭都面临着一个严重的威胁，那就是烹饪所需的煤球价格不断上涨。新的纪录价格是每吨265美元。华人圈子担心，除非停止对这种重要商品和日常必需品的投机，否则价格可能会达到每担15美元的最高点。战前价格低于每担1美元。除了担心每天的口粮大米外，穷人还在所有街道上寻找木柴，经常可以看到小贩出售看似被砍成小块的棺材碎片。

在沪华人普遍认为，与大米情况一样，煤球情况的严重性也已达到顶峰，中文报刊指控投机者在煤炭市场非常活跃，而当局正在寻求改善大米状况的补救措施。据说，他们的采购活动以及煤商所谓的囤积行为是价格上涨的主要原因。面对来自华人各界的强烈批评，机制煤球同业公会正计划召开会议讨论这一局势。

然而，据了解，与大米价格一样，煤炭价格也受到运费以及各煤球制造工厂维持工人成本增加的严重影响。降低运费再次是解决这一问题的一个非常重要的因素。制造煤球所需的材料持续运抵，现有库存超过30,000吨，足够一个月的消费量。这里每天大约售出1,000吨。

COAL SITUATION

The coal situation in Shanghai has undergone a big change since the last report on the subject and a review of the position at the present time does not reveal a very encouraging state of affairs.

As has been reported in previous reports, the difficulty in obtaining the necessary shipping facilities is the main factor contributing to the present unsatisfactory state of affairs. Steamers are now practically impossible to obtain and with certain ships being withdrawn from their normal trade, a serious deficiency in transport is being created. Just how and when a means of overcoming this deficiency will present itself is impossible to forecast.

It is perhaps as well to mention at this point that certain local importers have declared themselves unwilling to negotiate for steamers which are at present engaged in transporting rice, as it is felt that a shortage of rice in Shanghai will present a more serious condition locally than a shortage of coal.

The recent articles, referring to the Power Company, that have appeared in the local press have caused considerable consternation amongst local dealers, who have been endeavouring to buy up stocks far in excess of their normal requirements, since the publication of the articles. Should they have been successful in their efforts to accumulate large reserve stocks, the position that would ensue in the course of the next two or three months is not hard to guess. With imports reduced to a minimum and the existing stocks in the hands of a group of unscrupulous merchants, these same merchants would be in a position to dictate their own terms to consumers. These press articles have no doubt been justified to a certain extent, but it does seem as if they have done quite an amount of harm to a large extent unnecessarily. Although the position as outlined in the press is in the main correct, a more modified account of the state of affairs would have justified itself in that it very possibly would not have given rise to the state of anxiety prevailing at present.

To return to the shipping question, it would appear that with certain imports assured for March and April, the month of May will be a crucial month. Existing stocks in Shanghai with the arrivals for the next two months, will suffice for some time but unless a solution of the transport problem is found, it may well be that May will find the coal situation in Shanghai very difficult. One thing that seems assured is that prices will register an increase.

With regards to briquettes, rumours that have circulated regarding adulteration of the coal dust used are largely unconfirmed. It has been ascertained that a certain amount of cheap Japanese coal dust was acquired by briquette manufacturers and mixed with Hongay dust, thus keeping the price of briquettes down. Stocks of this cheaper dust have now been exhausted and an increase in the price of briquettes is a distinct possibility. However, it would appear that rumours of mud being mixed with the coal dust in greater proportion than usual are without foundation. Should the manufacturers not have used a certain amount of cheap coal dust, briquette prices would have increased by more than the $10 per ton already registered.

煤炭形势

自上次关于此主题的报告以来，上海的煤炭形势发生了巨大变化，对当前局势的审视并未显示出令人鼓舞的状况。

正如先前报告所述，难以获得必要的航运设施是导致目前这种令人不满状况的主要因素。目前实际上已无法租用到轮船，加之某些船只撤出正常贸易航线，造成了严重的运输短缺。究竟以何种方式、在何时会出现克服这一短缺的办法，目前无法预测。

在此或许值得提及，某些本地进口商已表示不愿洽谈那些目前正用于运输大米的轮船，因为人们认为，上海的大米短缺将比煤炭短缺在当地造成更严重的局面。

近期当地报刊上刊登的涉及电力公司的文章，在当地商人中引起了相当大的恐慌；自这些文章发表以来，商人们一直试图购入远超其正常需求的库存。如果他们在积累大量储备库存方面的努力取得成功，那么在未来两三个月内随之出现的局面是不难猜想的。随着进口量降至最低限度，而现有库存掌握在一群无良商人手中，这些商人将处于能够向消费者强加其自身条件的地位。这些报刊文章无疑在一定程度上是有根据的，但看来它们在很大程度上造成了不必要的损害。虽然报刊所概述的形势大体正确，但如果对事态进行更为温和的描述，本可证明其合理性，因为那样很可能不会引起目前普遍存在的焦虑状态。

回到航运问题，鉴于三月和四月的某些进口已有保障，五月将成为一个关键月份。上海现有的库存加上未来两个月的到货量，足以维持一段时间，但除非找到解决运输问题的办法，否则五月份上海的煤炭形势很可能会变得非常困难。有一件事似乎是确定的，那就是价格将出现上涨。

关于煤球，有关所用煤粉掺假的传闻大多未经证实。经查实，煤球制造商确实购买了一定数量的廉价日本煤粉，并将其与鸿基（Hongay）煤粉混合，从而压低了煤球的价格。目前这种较便宜煤粉的库存已耗尽，煤球价格上涨的可能性很大。然而，有关煤粉中混入泥土的比例高于往常的传闻似乎并无根据。如果制造商没有使用一定数量的廉价煤粉，煤球价格的涨幅将超过目前已记录的每吨10美元。

REPORT

S.1., Special Branch Station. File No.................... Date March 10, 1941.

SUBJECT:
Coal Situation

The coal situation in Shanghai has undergone a big change since the last report on the subject and a review of the position at the present time does not reveal a very encouraging state of affairs.

As has been reported in previous reports, the difficulty in obtaining the necessary shipping facilities is the main factor contributing to the present unsatisfactory state of affairs. Steamers are now practically impossible to obtain and with certain ships being withdrawn from their normal trade, a serious deficiency in transport is being created. Just how and when a means of overcoming this deficiency will present itself is impossible to forecast.

It is perhaps as well to mention at this point that certain local importers have declared themselves unwilling to negotiate for steamers which are at present engaged in transporting rice, as it is felt that a shortage of rice in Shanghai will present a more serious condition locally than a shortage of coal.

The recent notices, originating from the Power Company, that have appeared in the local press have caused considerable consternation amongst local dealers, who have been endeavouring to buy up stocks far in excess of their normal requirements, since the publication of the articles. Should they have been successful in their efforts to accumulate large reserve stocks, the position that would ensue in the course of the next two or three months is not hard to guess.

Date November 6, 1940.

Subject Coal Situation.

Made by D.P.S. Killingbeck Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

The only outstanding feature of the coal market at the end of October appears to be a considerable decrease in the arrivals of anthracite coal from Indo-China. This was brought about by the impossibility of obtaining the necessary shipping facilities. While only 9,600 tons arrived during October, it is hoped that the position will be improved during November as charters have been obtained on a few ships sailing under Panamanian and French flags. Previously, British ships were almost exclusively used in this, but they are now unavailable owing to the present situation in Indo-China. Freight charges, however, are very high on the ships obtained and it is expected that the price of anthracite coals will register an increase in the future.

Bituminous coals continue to arrive as usual, the arrivals for October being slightly more than for the previous month.

It appears that there is a shortage in the supply of briquettes as many of the briquette manufacturers have been unable to obtain sufficient quantities of coal dust, but this position will no doubt also be improved with the arrival of new stocks from Indo-China.

Following are the arrival for October:
Bituminous coals.
Poshan & Luta 30,700 Tons.

（印：MUNICIPAL POLICE / File Registry / D. 7557 / 9/40）
Date September 4, 1940.

Subject Coal Situation.

Made by D.P.S. Killingbeck. Forwarded by D. S. I. Logan.

The end of August finds the coal market
in Shanghai in a very quiet state, with not very
much business being transacted.
Although the imports of bituminous coals
during August are considerably lower than imports
for the month previous, the stocks at present in
Shanghai register an increase over figures for the
end of July.
A contributing factor to this state of
affairs is the Japanese naval blockade of China
coast ports. Ships usually plying between
Shanghai and the blockaded ports are at present
out of service and large quantities of bunker coal
remain unsold. There is also a noticeable
decrease in the consumption of coal by large
manufacturing concerns, as they are now unable to
do business with the districts served by the ports
which have now been closed to traffic. Whilst
on the subject of shipping, the belief is circulating
that Japanese interests are endeavouring to obtain
charters on shipping now lying idle, the ships
concerned being mostly under the register of small
foreign countries. It is thought that if this
attempt is successful, the Japanese authorities
will open the ports to trade again, but will by

decrease in the consumption of coal by large

do business with the districts served by the ports
which have now been closed to traffic. Whilst
on the subject of shipping, the belief is circulating
that Japanese interests are endeavouring to obtain
charters on shipping now lying idle, the ships
concerned being mostly under the register of small
foreign countries. It is thought that if this

煤炭情况。
40年9月4日。

八月底，上海煤炭市场处于非常沉寂的状态，交易不多。
尽管八月份烟煤进口量远低于前一个月，但上海目前的库存较七月底的数据有所增加。
造成这种状况的一个因素是日本海军对中国沿海港口的封锁。通常在上海与被封锁港口之间航行的船只目前停航，大量船用煤滞销。大型制造企业的煤炭消耗量也明显下降，因为它们现在无法与那些已关闭交通的港口所服务的地区进行贸易。在航运方面，流传着一种说法，即日本势力正试图包租目前闲置的船只，这些船只大多注册在小外国名下。人们认为，如果这一尝试成功，日本当局将重新开放港口进行贸易，但将通过

pages.en:
- 2 -

then have a controlling interest in trading.
During March and April, large quantities
of coal were ordered by dealers who had hoped for
good market in Shanghai owing to the threatened
shortage. These stocks, which arrived in Shanghai
during June, July and August, are now not in demand
and cases have been noticed where dealers have
quoted prices for imported coal which are in some
instances less than the actual cost prices. Other
merchants no doubt hope to obtain better prices
during the winter months but will in all probability
only manage to recover the initial costs, with
small, or no, margin of profit.
The anthracite coal market continues
about the same, with prices slightly changed.
Business in "briquettes" is very slack.

Coal Situation.

The coal situation prevailing in Shanghai at the end of June does not call for much comment and, but for the present high price of the commodity, can be described as normal at the present time.

It will be remembered that mention was made in the last report on the coal situation, of the importation of anthracite coals from Korea. It has since been learned that this forms part of an amount of 100,000 tons which a Japanese concern, the M.S.K. has contracted to import from Korea during the Summer months, from May to October. The amount of Korean anthracite imported during June is 16,200 tons. Subsequent enquiries tend to confirm the opinion expressed in the report dated June 6, that this is an inferior grade of coal and is being sold at a cheap rate to Japanese consumers.

As it is at the present impossible to state just what the final outcome of the threatened trouble in South China and Indo-China will be, no comment can be made as to how the coal situation will be affected in the event of future developments in those areas.

During past months, ships engaged in transporting coal for the K.M.A. and Shanghai Power Company have been requisitioned by H.B.M. Government, but have since been released to carry on their normal trade.

煤炭形势。

六月底上海 prevailing 的煤炭形势无需过多评论，除了该商品目前价格高企外，目前可描述为正常。

记得在上一份关于煤炭形势的报告中曾提到从朝鲜进口无烟煤一事。后获悉，这是日本公司 M.S.K.  contracted 在夏季月份（五月至十月）从朝鲜进口的10万吨煤炭的一部分。六月份进口的朝鲜无烟煤数量为16,200吨。随后的调查倾向于证实6月6日报告中表达的观点，即这是一种劣质煤，并以低廉的价格出售给日本消费者。

由于目前无法确切说明华南及印度支那地区 threatened 的动荡最终结果如何，因此无法就这些地区未来事态发展将如何影响煤炭形势发表评论。

CHINA PRESS.
MAY 1940

Coal Dust Quoted In U.S.
Currency On Local Market

Considerable uneasiness was noted in local commodity trading yesterday when the Shanghai Coal Dealers Guild announced that henceforth coal dust prices would be quoted in U.S. dollars.

The price quoted yesterday was US$7 per ton. It was stated, however, that the quotation would follow closely the day-to-day variations of the value of the Chinese dollar.

Coal dust, traders pointed out, is a required product in the manufacture of coal briquettes, used generally by the city's poor.

Expressing amazement at the ruling, coal briquette manufacturers yesterday stated that the measure might put a number of small briquette makers out of existence since it would strip the business of every possibility of profit.

A ton of coal dust, a manufacturer asserted, is sufficient to produce about 20 piculs of briquettes. Retailers now are asking about $9 for each picul.

At the prevailing rate of exchange, it was stated, a ton of coal dust costs about $150. This means that raw product alone would cost the briquette maker nearly $7.50 per picul.

Officials of the Guild, in announcing the new regulation, again blamed hoarders for the constantly mounting cost of coal briquettes. They asserted that if hoarders unload their holdings, the price of briquettes, despite the exchange crisis, would greatly ease.

The price of rice, on the other hand, showed a slight improvement as compared with Monday. A general decline of about $1 was noted in the price of both domestic and Saigon rice.

1940年5月

本地市场以美元报价煤屑

昨日，上海煤业公会宣布此后煤屑价格将以美元报价，本地商品交易因此出现相当程度的不安。

昨日报价为每吨7美元。但据称，该报价将紧随法币（中国元）价值的每日波动。

贸易商指出，煤屑是制造煤球的必需原料，而煤球通常为城市贫民所使用。

煤球制造商昨日对该规定表示惊讶，并称此举可能会使许多小型煤球制造商破产，因为它将剥夺该行业所有的获利可能。

一位制造商声称，一吨煤屑足以生产约20担煤球。目前零售商每担售价约为9美元。

据称，按现行汇率计算，一吨煤屑成本约为150美元。这意味着仅原材料一项，煤球制造商每担的成本就接近7.50美元。

公会在宣布新规定时，再次指责囤积者导致煤球价格不断上涨。他们断言，如果囤积者抛售存货，尽管存在汇兑危机，煤球价格也将大幅回落。

另一方面，与周一相比，米价略有改善。国产米和西贡米的价格均出现约1美元的普遍下跌。

Coal Situation

The most important feature of the Coal Situation locally at the present time is a further increase in prices brought about by the sudden fluctuation of the local dollar. On May 3, Calcutta coal was quoted on the retail market at from $305 - $310 per ton and anthracite from $190 - $220 per ton but it is impossible to forecast what the immediate future will bring forth as far as coal prices are concerned.

Arrivals for the month of April are larger than for the month previous, the relative figures for import of bituminous coals being 152,200 tons during March as against 199,600 tons for the month of April. Indian coal continues to arrive in Shanghai, the larger part of stocks being for the Shanghai Power Company.

Messrs. Jardine Matheson are importing stocks of coal from Calcutta as are a few of the local Chinese dealers. Included in the imports from Calcutta for April are also 7,600 tons for the M.B.K.

With reference to the attached cutting from the "Evening Echo" dated April 19, 1940 the majority of the ships mentioned are on charter to the Shanghai Power Company. Large Quantities Of
Coal Being Sent Here

Reports to the effect that Shang-
hai will face a serious shortage of
coal because no ship will be avail-
able for the transporting of coal to
Shanghai following the extension of
the European conflict are denied by
well-informed shipping circles, as
large numbers of ships are on their
way to Shanghai, bringing with
them large quantities of coal.
The s.s. Jeannette Skinner of the
Jardine Matheson Co., bringing
with it 7,090 tons of coal will arrive
here in a day or two from Calcutta.
The s.s. Marion Moller will arrive
today with 5,563 tons of coal from
Calcutta. The s.s. Stagen of the
Java-China-Japan Lijn will arrive
on April 22 with large quantities of
coal from Haiphong. The s.s. Liliam
Moller will bring here 7,000 tons of
coal on April 23.
The Therese Moller will bring
here 546 tons of coal on April 25.
The s.s. Gladys Moller will bring
7,020 tons and the Daisy Moller will
bring also a large quantity of coal
here on April 26. On April 29 the
s.s. Helene Moller will bring here
6,476 tons of coal. In addition, a
number of other ships loaded with
coal will arrive here soon, but their
names were not divulged by the
shipping companies.
So far as generally known, no less
than 36,000 tons of coal are on the
way and will arrive here before the
end of this month. With the arrival
of this large quantity of coal, there
is no reason for any increase of the
price of coal in the local market.

《晚声报》
1940年4月19日

大量煤炭
正运往此地

航运界消息灵通人士否认了有关上海将面临严重煤炭短缺的报道，这些报道声称，随着欧洲冲突的扩大，将没有船只可用于向上海运输煤炭。事实上，大量船只正驶往上海，载有大量煤炭。
怡和洋行的“Jeannette Skinner”号轮船载有7,090吨煤炭，将在这一两天内从加尔各答抵达此处。“Marion Moller”号轮船今天将抵达，载有来自加尔各答的5,563吨煤炭。爪哇-中国-日本航线的“Stagen”号轮船将于4月22日抵达，载有大量来自海防的煤炭。“Liliam Moller”号轮船将于4月23日在此卸下7,000吨煤炭。
“Therese Moller”号轮船将于4月25日在此卸下546吨煤炭。“Gladys Moller”号轮船将运载7,020吨，“Daisy Moller”号轮船也将于4月26日在此卸下大量煤炭。4月29日，“Helene Moller”号轮船将在此卸下6,476吨煤炭。此外，还有多艘装载煤炭的其他船只即将抵达此处，但航运公司未透露其名称。
据一般了解，不少于36,000吨煤炭正在途中，并将在本月底前抵达此处。随着这批大量煤炭的抵达，本地市场的煤炭价格没有理由上涨。

Coal Situation
--------------

The local coal situation at the beginning of March does not appear to have altered much from that prevailing at the beginning of February, 1940.

One notable feature, however, is the fact that shipments of Indian coal have been brought into Shanghai for general use, apart from the usual consignments for the Shanghai Power Company. It is expected that one ship will be arriving each month with stocks of Indian coal. The importers will endeavour to maintain a fixed price for this coal over a period of three or four months, but whether this will actually prove possible depends on the shipments arriving regularly without loss. The price will in all probability be considerably less than the $280.00 per ton quoted in some circles recently. This figure does not represent a true price and was no doubt the result of a very urgent demand for available supplies.

February arrivals of bituminous coals register an increase on the figures for January arrivals, the relevant figures being 102,300 tons and 96,600 tons respectively. The renewed imports of coal from India account for the increase.

There are still sufficient stocks of anthracite coal arriving in Shanghai to satisfy normal requirements, but there is a marked tendency on the part of consumers to order larger quantities of coal than usual, in order to ensure sufficient stocks for some time to come. These increased orders are not being filled, the supply to individual consumers being limited to one ton at a time by some dealers. Exceptions to this procedure are made in the case of regular customers who have in the past been purchasing larger quantities.

One point that must not be overlooked at this time is that most of the ships at present engaged in transporting coal from

煤炭情况
--------------

3月初的本地煤炭情况似乎与1940年2月初的情况相比没有太大变化。

然而，一个显著的特点是，除了通常供应给上海电力公司的货物外，印度煤炭的装运也已进入上海供一般使用。预计每月将有一艘载有印度煤炭库存的船只抵达。进口商将努力在三四个月内维持该煤炭的固定价格，但这是否真的可行，取决于货物能否定期无损地抵达。价格很可能远低于近期某些圈子所报价的每吨280.00元。这个数字并不代表真实价格，无疑是由于对现有供应的迫切需求所致。

2月份烟煤的到货量较1月份的数字有所增加，相关数字分别为102,300吨和96,600吨。从印度重新进口煤炭是增加的原因。

目前仍有足够的无烟煤运抵上海以满足正常需求，但消费者明显倾向于订购比平时更多的煤炭，以确保未来一段时间内有足够的库存。这些增加的订单并未得到满足，一些经销商将向个别消费者的供应量限制为每次一吨。对于过去一直购买较大数量的常规客户，则对此程序予以例外处理。

此时不可忽视的一点是，目前大多数从事从

Confidential
The Kailan Mining Administration,
Shanghai, 5th. March, 1940.

The Assistant Secretary.

Dear Mr. Nash,

I have received your letter F 50/12 of February 28th regarding the possibility of adopting measures to limit the prices of coal and briquettes in the Settlement.

I would like to say at once that the idea seems to me to be excellent, but you, with the experience gained in respect of controlling the rice situation, must know far more about the possibility of its success than I. Nevertheless I should be very glad to help in any way I can and I should be very interested to hear how you would propose setting about it.

I think the only thing that I can do for the time being is to comment on the enclosures sent with your letter, as in certain respects the remarks contained therein are not quite accurate. The fact that it now costs well over $200 a ton to import coal from India has raised the market price of all coals to this level, and the public and the press have both assumed that because prices are high there must be profiteering. There is, of course, profiteering in coal, but every ton that is sold at $300 has not necessarily been profiteered on. It is also assumed that local dealers are holding up large stocks of coal currently required for consumption, and thereby forcing prices to the present extraordinary heights. This again is only partly true.

For the last four months I estimate that the consumption of Shanghai has been around 200,000 tons a month, of which we have supplied about 47%. Actual figures are as follows:-

| | Shanghai Consumption | K.M.A. Sales | K.M.A. Percentage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| October | 139,000 | 90,100 | 47.6 |
| November | 185,000 | 91,300 | 49.2 |
| December | 210,000 | 93,300 | 44.5 |
| January | 207,000 | 97,700 | 46.9 |
| | 791,000 | 372,400 | |

Our sales to dealers amount to 4,500 tons a month, say 5% of our business, or taking the average of 200,000 tons for local consumption, 2% of the market. The emphasis laid on the high prices being asked by dealers is, therefore, in my opinion, exaggerated, as only a small - but apparently rather vociferous - section of the community is touched. As sales of coal other than Kailan are very small at present, I should think that actually not more than 3% of this market's consumption is being supplied with this "profiteering" coal.

This brings me to a phrase I noted in the reports, and that is - "K.M.A's authorized dealers". In the sense that the three firms named are the only dealers to whom we supply coal, they may be described as authorised, but they are separate concerns who follow their own line of business without any control from us. We have been doing business with these people for many years, and it was decided in the winter of 1937/38 that we should continue to keep them going as long as we are able to import coal.
pages.zh:
机密
开滦矿务局，
上海，1940年3月5日。

致助理秘书。

亲爱的纳什先生：

我已收到你2月28日关于在租界采取限制煤炭和煤球价格措施的可能性的F 50/12号来信。

我首先要说，这个想法在我看来极好，但你凭借在控制大米局势方面获得的经验，对其成功的可能性肯定比我了解得多。尽管如此，我非常乐意尽我所能提供帮助，并且很有兴趣听听你打算如何着手进行。

我想目前我唯一能做的就是对你随信附上的文件发表评论，因为其中的某些评论并不完全准确。现在从印度进口煤炭的成本远高于每吨200元，这一事实已将所有煤炭的市场价格推高至这一水平，公众和媒体都假设因为价格高，就一定存在牟取暴利行为。当然，煤炭行业存在牟取暴利的现象，但并非每一吨以300元售出的煤炭都一定含有暴利。人们还假设本地经销商囤积了大量目前消费所需的煤炭库存，从而迫使价格达到目前的异常高位。这也只是部分属实。

据我估计，在过去四个月里，上海的月消费量约为20万吨，其中我们供应了约47%。实际数字如下：-

| | 上海消费量 | 开滦矿务局销量 | 开滦矿务局占比 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 十月 | 139,000 | 90,100 | 47.6 |
| 十一月 | 185,000 | 91,300 | 49.2 |
| 十二月 | 210,000 | 93,300 | 44.5 |
| 一月 | 207,000 | 97,700 | 46.9 |
| | 791,000 | 372,400 | |

我们要向经销商销售的量为每月4,500吨，约占我们业务的5%，或者按本地平均消费量20万吨计算，占市场的2%。因此，我认为强调经销商索要高价是被夸大了，因为只有社区中一小部分——尽管显然相当喧闹——的人群受到影响。由于目前除开滦煤以外的其他煤炭销售量非常小，我认为实际上只有不超过3%的市场消费量是由这种“牟取暴利”的煤炭供应的。

这就引出了我在报告中注意到的一个短语，即——“开滦矿务局的授权经销商”。如果说这三家指定的公司是我们供应煤炭的唯一经销商，他们可以被称为授权经销商，但他们是独立的实体，按照自己的业务路线经营，不受我们的任何控制。我们与这些人做生意已有多年，并在1937/38年冬季决定，只要我们能进口煤炭，就继续维持他们的运营。

pages.en:
2.

As you must realise, we ourselves have given considerable thought to this business of controlling outside prices, as we are in part responsible in that we make coal available to be sold. We came to the conclusion some time ago, and I think it is still correct, that given the fact that we supply any coal to the outside market, it is impossible to control selling prices while there is a shortage, and the only way to limit dealers' profits is by cutting down the tonnage available for them. This has been done, and I give below figures showing supplies that we have made to dealers for the past five or six years:-

1934 563,078 tons
1935 550,202
1936 227,592
1937 228,966
1938 120,555
1939 77,714
1940 (estimate) 50/55,000

Provided we continue doing business with dealers I do not think we can reduce the 1940 estimate, which works out at only 1,500 tons to each of the three dealers per month.

As far as price is concerned, there is a law of supply and demand and in certain trades, particularly shipping, the whole basis of price fixing is what the charterer will pay. I personally agree with you that profiteering should be checked but cannot see how it can be done in one trade and not in another, although as I have said above, I should be very glad if I could help to institute some sort of control. In this particular case I can think of no argument to convince a Chinese dealer that he should sell coal at say $100 or $150 a ton when he knows that outside $200 or $220 can be obtained; moreover that it is almost a certainty that the people to whom he sells at the lower figure will immediately go outside to resell. There is a further point: that as far as we are concerned, these dealers handle business and supply sections of the community which we cannot and do not want to supply.

Although we sell a certain amount of household coal in one ton lots, we are not anxious to deal in small tonnages and we are not organized for it. Dealers will supply any quantity, from a basket upwards, and will moreover give credit where we could not dream of doing so. The hot water shops, who seem to be getting a good deal of mention in this correspondence, is a type of business that we never used to deal with ourselves, although a few months ago we did start a system of registration with the idea of trying to supply direct to a few of the more reputable ones. The idea was not altogether a success, as these shops soon got under the control of small coal brokers, and they were in fact among the first to start reselling our coal rather than using it for their normal business.

To deal with other points made in the enclosures to your letter -

(1) Indian coal, it is true, has gone up a great deal in price, but I do not think the figure of $280 a ton quoted is a representative one, in fact I would definitely say it is much too high. $220 to $240 is a much fairer figure, and as you may have heard, we ourselves are selling
pages.zh:
2.

正如阁下所意识到的，我们自己也已对控制外部市场价格这一事务给予了相当多的考虑，因为我们在提供煤炭以供销售方面负有部分责任。我们前一段时间得出的结论是——我认为该结论目前仍然正确——鉴于我们确实向外部市场供应任何煤炭的事实，在短缺情况下不可能控制销售价格，而限制经销商利润的唯一途径是减少可供他们销售的吨位。此项措施已付诸实施，下文列出了过去五六年间我们向经销商提供的供应量数据：-

1934年 563,078吨
1935年 550,202
1936年 227,592
1937年 228,966
1938年 120,555
1939年 77,714
1940年（预估） 50/55,000

只要我们继续与经销商开展业务，我认为我们无法进一步降低1940年的预估值，该数值折算下来仅为每家经销商每月1,500吨。

就价格而言，存在供需法则，而在某些行业，特别是航运业，定价的整个基础在于承租人的支付意愿。我个人同意阁下关于应当遏制牟取暴利的观点，但看不出如何能在一个行业中做到这一点而在另一个行业中却做不到，尽管如上所述，若我能协助建立某种形式的管控机制，我将非常乐意。在此特定案例中，我想不出任何论据能说服中国经销商以每吨100或150美元的价格出售煤炭，因为他知道在外部市场可以获得200或220美元；此外，几乎可以肯定的是，那些以较低价格从他手中购买煤炭的人会立即转手到外部市场进行倒卖。还有一点：就我方而言，这些经销商所处理的业务及所服务的社区部分，是我们无法且不愿直接供应的。

虽然我们以一吨为单位出售一定数量的家用煤，但我们并不热衷于处理小批量交易，也未为此做好组织准备。经销商可以供应从一篮起的任意数量，而且还能提供赊销服务，这是我们做梦也想不到的。在本函件往来中被多次提及的热水店（hot water shops），是一种我们过去从未直接打交道的商业类型，尽管几个月前我们确实启动了一项登记制度，试图直接向其中几家信誉较好的店铺供货。这一设想并未完全成功，因为这些店铺很快就被小型煤炭经纪人所控制，事实上，它们是最早开始转售我方煤炭而非将其用于正常营业的群体之一。

针对阁下信函附件中提出的其他几点——

(1) 印度煤炭的价格确实大幅上涨，但我认为引用的每吨280美元这一数字并不具有代表性，实际上我可以明确地说，该价格过高。220至240美元是一个更为公平的数字，而且正如阁下可能已听闻，我们自己正在以

pages.en:
3.

it at £215. Of course some of these prices are, in a way,
a ramp, as with the exception of the Power Company and our-
selves, nobody has imported Indian coal recently and these
high figures are being asked for coal that has been in
stock since last year when the cost of importing was prob-
ably not more than $30 a ton, and therefore the only way
these prices can be justified is on their replacement value.
Nevertheless supplies of this old coal are very limited,
and I should think by the end of this month they will be
exhausted altogether.

In any question of fixing prices I think one must
take a very different attitude with regard to Indian coal
to Kailan. Kailan coal is sold on an ex-wharf or ex-yard
basis, and the purchaser therefore has absolutely no risk
to take. The responsibility of a shipper of Indian coal
starts when the vessel sails from Calcutta, and especially
at present he can be by no means sure that it will arrive
safely or that he will not be involved in extra expenses
en route. The legitimate profit on these two types of
coal is therefore very different, and should be allowed
for.

(2) Monopoly I make no comment on, but if the cost
given in your report and the prices are correct, there
does not seem to be much abuse here.

(3) As to the hoarding of coal, I cannot say any-
thing definite. My own opinion is that there is probably
not very much being indulged in. Coal is a large commodity
to store and is difficult to conceal. Moreover storing of
coal by factories is a legitimate process, and in many cases
the coal in yards has already been sold and is being held
there for consumers who have only limited stocking space.

Yours sincerely,

L. Handley-Terry

S.T. Hess, Esq.,
Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.
pages.zh:
3.

215英镑的价格出售。当然，从某种意义上说，这些价格带有哄抬性质，因为除了电力公司和我们自己之外，最近没有人进口印度煤炭，而这些高价是针对自去年以来一直库存的煤炭提出的，当时的进口成本可能不超过每吨30美元，因此，证明这些价格合理性的唯一依据是其重置价值。尽管如此，这类旧煤的供应量非常有限，我认为到本月底它们将完全耗尽。

在任何关于定价的问题上，我认为对于印度煤炭和开滦煤炭必须采取截然不同的态度。开滦煤炭是按码头交货或堆场交货 basis 出售的，因此买方绝对不承担任何风险。印度煤炭发货人的责任始于船只从加尔各答启航之时，特别是在当前形势下，他绝不能保证货物能安全抵达，也不能保证途中不会产生额外费用。因此，这两类煤炭的合理利润差异很大，应当予以考虑。

(2) 关于垄断问题，我不予置评，但如果阁下报告中给出的成本和价格是正确的，那么这里似乎没有太多的滥用行为。

(3) 关于囤积煤炭一事，我无法给出确切的说法。我个人的看法是，此类行为可能并不普遍。煤炭是一种体积庞大的商品，难以隐藏。此外，工厂储存煤炭是一个合法的过程，在许多情况下，堆场中的煤炭已经售出，只是代为持有，供那些仓储空间有限的消费者提取。

此致

敬礼

L. Handley-Terry

S.T. Hess 先生，
工部局，
上海。

Extract from North China Daily News dated March 6, 1940.

COAL SITUATION SHOWS IMPROVEMENT

Large Imports Swell City's Available Stocks.

An optimistic tone was struck by the Chinese press yesterday regarding the coal situation in Shanghai, it being asserted that there is much ready stock and that new supplies are arriving. . It is pointed out that during January alone Shanghai imported more than 200,000 tons of coal amounting to more than $3,400,000.

There are between 500,000 and 600,000 tons of coal stored in various godowns in the city, including those in Pootung. Negotiations for buying 100,000 tons of coal from India and Annam have been successfully concluded and the coal will gradually arrive here after the middle of this month, it is stated.

It is indicated in the reports that merchants who have been hoarding coal have been much discouraged and that the coal market here is returning to normal. A French Concession coal shop which has sold coal at a price higher than the one prevailing in the cheap sale market (for the poor) has been officially warned by the Chinese Chamber of Commerce here.
pages.zh:
摘自1940年3月6日《字林西报》。

煤炭形势显示改善

大量进口增加城市可用库存。

中国报纸昨日对上海的煤炭形势持乐观态度，声称现有大量现货，且新货源正在运抵。报道指出，仅在一月份，上海就进口了超过20万吨煤炭，价值超过340万美元。

据称，包括浦东在内的全市各仓库中储存有50万至60万吨煤炭。从印度和安南（Annam）购买10万吨煤炭的谈判已成功结束，这批煤炭将在本月月中旬后陆续运抵此处。

报道表明，一直囤积煤炭的商人受到了极大打击，这里的煤炭市场正回归正常。法租界一家以高于廉价市场（面向穷人） prevailing price 的价格出售煤炭的煤店，已受到上海总商会的正式警告。

pages.en:
Coal Situation
--------------

The local coal situation at the beginning of
March does not appear to have altered much from that
prevailing at the beginning of February, 1940.

One notable feature, however, is the fact
that shipments of Indian coal have been brought into
Shanghai for general use, apart from the usual consign-
ments for the Shanghai Power Company. It is expected
that one ship will be arriving each month with stocks
of Indian coal. The importers will endeavour to
maintain a fixed price for this coal over a period of
three or four months, but whether this will actually
prove possible depends on the shipments arriving regular-
ly without loss. The price will in all probability
be considerably less than the $280.00 per ton quoted
in some circles recently. This figure does not
represent a true price and was no doubt the result of
a very urgent demand for available supplies.

February arrivals of bituminous coals register
an increase on the figures for January arrivals, the
relevant figures being 102,300 tons and 96,600 tons
respectively. The renewed imports of coal from
India account for the increase.

There are still sufficient stocks of anthracite
coal arriving in Shanghai to satisfy normal requirements,
but there is a marked tendency on the part of consumers
to order larger quantities of coal than usual, in order
to ensure sufficient stocks for some time to come.
pages.zh:
煤炭形势
--------------

3月初的本地煤炭形势与1940年2月初的情况相比，似乎没有太大变化。

然而，一个显著的特点是，除了通常供应给上海电力公司的货物外，印度煤炭的船运货物已进入上海供一般使用。预计每月将有一艘载有印度煤炭库存的船只抵达。进口商将努力在三到四个月内维持该煤炭的固定价格，但这是否真的可行，取决于货物能否定期无损地抵达。价格极有可能远低于近期某些圈子中引用的每吨280.00美元。这一数字并不代表真实价格，无疑是由于对现有供应的迫切需求所致。

2月份烟煤的抵达量较1月份的数字有所增加，相关数据分别为102,300吨和96,600吨。煤炭进口的恢复主要来自印度，这解释了增长的原因。

仍有充足的无烟煤库存运抵上海以满足正常需求，但消费者明显倾向于订购比平时更大数量的煤炭，以确保未来一段时间内有足够的库存。

Police Report, February 5, 1940.

Coal Situation.

The condition of the local coal market at the end
of January 1940 remains very unsatisfactory and, if anything,
slightly worse than was the case at the end of last year.

Imports of bituminous coal during January registered
a drop as compared with the figures for December, the relevant
figures being 96,600 tons and 109,200 tons respectively. As
the issues for the month of January total approximately
115,000 tons, stocks in Shanghai have been further depleted.
It is believed that some of the large industrial concerns in
Shanghai have been experiencing difficulty in obtaining
sufficient stocks of coal and unless the firms concerned decide
to undertake the importation of coal from India, at the present
high price, there does not seem to be any possibility of their
being able to obtain their normal requirements in the near
future. Certain of the firms affected, whose plants are able
to operate on 'hard' coal, have applied to Messrs. Hongay Coal
Sales Ltd. for supplies of Anthracite, but were unable to obtain
any. Messrs. Hongay Ltd. are not prepared to supply large
consumers at the expense of their regular customers. They still
are able to meet the demands of their customers and announce
that there is at present no reason why small consumers should
find any difficulty in obtaining supplies of Anthracite coal.

It is interesting to note that Messrs. Hongay Coal
Sales Ltd. have recently supplied some 500 tons of coal to one
or two French missions in the Hankow region. This creates
something of a precedent, as these missions have up till the
present been able to obtain supplies direct from North China.

The fact that there is a coal shortage in Japan will
no doubt affect the local market, as the Japanese Cabinet have
agreed to allow the importation of foreign coal as an emergency
measure. A certain percentage of this coal will be obtained
from North China and Manchukuo, thus further curtailing stocks
that would normally be available for Shanghai consumption.
This information is contained in a report, published in the
"Shanghai Sunday Times", dated January 28, 1940. Certain local
coal dealers have agreed that this position will eventuate, but
express the belief that the figures quoted are smaller than
they actually will be.

With reference to the importation of Indian coal by
certain large coal firms in Shanghai, it is learned that
Messrs. Nyi Tai Shing intend to import Indian coal, through
Messrs. Jinkee & Co., 100 Jinkee Road and the Yuan Tai Co. will
import stocks through Messrs. Jardine Matheson & Co. It will
be some time, however, before these stocks reach Shanghai.

Prices have registered further increases, the high
freight charges being to a large extent responsible. Follow-
ing are the imports of coal for January.

Poshan & Luta               14900   "

煤炭状况。

1940年1月底本地煤炭市场的状况仍然非常令人不满，甚至比去年年底的情况略糟。

一月份烟煤进口量较十二月份的数据有所下降，相关数据分别为 96,600 吨和 109,200 吨。由于一月份的发放总量约为 115,000 吨，上海的库存进一步消耗。据信，上海的一些大型工业企业一直在难以获得充足的煤炭库存，除非有关公司决定以目前的高价从印度进口煤炭，否则它们在近期似乎无法满足其正常需求。某些受影响的工厂能够使用“硬”煤运行，已向鸿基煤炭销售有限公司（Messrs. Hongay Coal Sales Ltd.）申请供应无烟煤，但未能获得任何供应。鸿基有限公司（Messrs. Hongay Ltd.）不愿以牺牲其常规客户为代价向大型消费者供货。他们仍能满足客户的需求，并宣称目前小型消费者在获取无烟煤供应方面没有任何理由遇到困难。

值得注意的是，鸿基煤炭销售有限公司最近向汉口地区的一两个法国传教团供应了约 500 吨煤炭。这开创了一个先例，因为这些传教团此前一直能够直接从华北获得供应。

日本存在煤炭短缺的事实无疑会影响本地市场，因为日本内阁已同意作为紧急措施允许进口外国煤炭。这部分煤炭中有一定比例将从华北和满洲国获得，从而进一步削减原本可供上海消费的库存。这一信息包含在1940年1月28日出版的《上海星期日报》（Shanghai Sunday Times）的一份报告中。某些本地煤炭经销商同意这一局面将会出现，但表示相信所引用的数字比实际数字要小。

关于上海某些大型煤炭公司进口印度煤炭一事，获悉义泰盛（Messrs. Nyi Tai Shing）打算通过金记洋行（Messrs. Jinkee & Co.，地址：金记路100号）进口印度煤炭，而源泰公司（Yuan Tai Co.）将通过怡和洋行（Messrs. Jardine Matheson & Co.）进口库存。然而，这些库存抵达上海尚需时日。

价格进一步上涨，高昂的运费在很大程度上是造成这一情况的原因。以下是一月份的煤炭进口情况。

URGENT
5 JAN 40
POLICE FORCE
FOR COMMENT
The Kailen Mining Administration.
Shanghai, 1st January 1940.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / CENTRAL REC. DIV. / I. 2836/1d 6(11) / 5 / 1 / 40）

Dear Mr. Nosh,

I would refer to my letter to you of November 14th commenting upon the Police Report for the month of October.

I am sorry to say that the fears which I expressed in this letter have materialized, and in my opinion we are at the beginning of a fairly serious coal shortage. At the moment it is impossible to give you facts or figures which will bear out my contention, but I feel that I should at least give you what information I have and let you know my view of the situation, which I hope you will check with any other sources of information that you may have.

As I pointed out on the second page of my letter; this market is dependent upon other sources of supply than the Administration for its coal and until recently it has been able to draw on Tsingtao, Japan and Calcutta for this balance. As I explained, in my opinion Indian coal would cease to come to this market, but what I could not be sure of was whether this source of supply would be replaced in any degree by the Shantung coal mines. I give you the figures of importations from these two sources for the past year and am presuming that the Shanghai Power Company will continue to import on the same scale during 1940. Nevertheless there is a balance of over 100,000 tons to be found and I do not know where it is coming from.

You will note that Tsingtao supplies are quite irregular in quantity and that recent shipments have been very much less than in the earlier part of the year.

There was however another unknown factor in the situation, and that was the general consumption of coal in Shanghai. When we had our meetings in September, and even at the time of writing to you last, I did not know what effect the European war would have on Far Eastern markets. I think at one of the meetings I raised this point of whether Shanghai manufacturers would be able to take advantage of the situation and supply goods for foreign consumption. I feel fairly certain now that foreign markets are looking and will look to China, and therefore to Shanghai, to supply a certain part of the goods which before came from Europe. Demand for coal from factories, therefore, should not in any way be diminished, but on the other hand will probably be increased during the coming year. You will no doubt be able to check from other sources as to how far I am correct in making this statement, but I am fairly sure that it is true.

Further, Japanese firms who in the past have supplied a certain amount of coal to the general market have now, I believe, had to concentrate entirely on the requirements of Japanese and Japanese-controlled factories, so that yet one more source of supply has now been withdrawn from the average consumer. Actually the amount from this source in the past was not very great, and the present restrictions imposed by the Japanese Coal Committee may well be withdrawn within a comparatively short time (though I doubt it). Here again you will probably be able to obtain more correct information than I have at my disposal.

（批：Noted 8/1/40. Greeningwood）

亲爱的纳什 (Nosh) 先生：

我谨提及我于11月14日致您的信，信中评论了十月份的警务报告。

我很遗憾地说，我在该信中表示的担忧已成为现实，而且在我看来，我们正处于相当严重的煤炭短缺的开端。目前，我无法向您提供能够证实我论点的事实或数据，但我觉得我至少应该向您提供我所掌握的信息，并让您了解我对局势的看法，希望您能与您可能拥有的其他信息来源进行核对。

正如我在信的第二页所指出的那样；本市场的煤炭供应依赖于管理局以外的其他来源，直到最近，它一直能够从青岛、日本和加尔各答获取这部分平衡供应。正如我所解释的，在我看来，印度煤炭将停止进入本市场，但我不能确定的是，山东煤矿能在多大程度上替代这一供应来源。我向您提供过去一年从这两个来源进口的数据，并假设上海电力公司将在1940年继续以相同的规模进口。尽管如此，仍有超过10万吨的缺口需要填补，而我不知道这些煤炭将从何而来。

您会注意到，青岛的供应量在数量上极不规律，且最近的出货量远少于年初。

然而，局势中还有另一个未知因素，那就是上海的煤炭总消费量。当我们在九月份举行会议时，甚至在我上次给您写信时，我都不知道欧洲战争会对远东市场产生什么影响。我想在一次会议上我曾提出过这一点，即上海制造商是否能够利用这一局势，为国外消费提供商品。我现在相当肯定，国外市场正在并将指望中国，因此也指望上海，来供应以前来自欧洲的部分商品。因此，工厂对煤炭的需求绝不应减少，反而可能在来年增加。您无疑能够从其他来源核实我这一说法的正确程度，但我相当确信这是真的。

此外，我认为过去向一般市场供应一定数量煤炭的日本公司，现在不得不完全专注于日本及日资控制工厂的需求，因此普通消费者又失去了一个供应来源。实际上，过去来自这一来源的数量并不大，而且日本煤炭委员会目前实施的限制很可能在相对较短的时间内解除（尽管我对此表示怀疑）。在这方面，您可能比我更能获得更准确的信息。

（批注：1940年1月8日阅知。Greeningwood）

pages.en:
3.

Nevertheless, broadly speaking, this is how the present
situation looks to me. Indian coal is ruled out except for the
Power Company, probably the Gas Company and possibly a combination
of big firms who might later on be forced by pressure of circum-
stances to import an odd shipment from time to time.

(2) Shantung fields cannot make up the quantity lost
from India, and in fact are barely coming up to their own estimates
made in September and October.

(5) The consumption requirements of the Japanese market
in Shanghai and the lower Yangtse have now increased considerably,
and it is therefore unlikely that they will have any surplus to
sell on the open market.

For the time being therefore, Keilan will be the only
coal for the general foreign and Chinese market, and in my opinion
we cannot possibly meet the demand. Our stock position is now a
little better than normal and supplies are coming in regularly,
nevertheless it is not possible to make one ton take the place of
two and already I am being told that unless I increase supplies
this or that factory will have to reduce operations or this or
that ship will not be able to run.

Moreover stocks of competitive coals have reached the
lowest point of which we have any record, with the exception of
four months in 1938 when the general situation was peculiar any-
way owing to local hostilities.

As I said in my other letter I believe that a good many
people have got reserves of coal in their yards, but when this is
finished I do not know how they can be replaced unless some steps
are taken in the near future to remedy the situation.

This is a gloomy picture I have painted for you on the
first day of the new year. I hope I may prove to be wrong.

Yours sincerely,

L. Handley-Terry

J.T. Nash, Esq.,
Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.
pages.zh:
3.

尽管如此， broadly speaking，这就是我对当前局势的看法。除了电力公司、可能是煤气公司以及可能是一些大公司组合（他们日后可能会因形势所迫而不时进口零星货物）外，印度煤炭已被排除在外。

(2) 山东矿区无法弥补从印度损失的产量，事实上，其产量 barely 达到其在九月和十月做出的自身估算。

(5) 上海及长江下游地区日本市场的消费需求现已大幅增加，因此他们不太可能有任何剩余产品在公开市场上出售。

因此，暂时而言，开滦煤炭将是面向一般外籍和华人市场的唯一煤炭，而且在我看来，我们根本无法满足需求。我们的库存状况现在比正常情况稍好，供应也定期进入，尽管如此，不可能让一吨煤发挥两吨煤的作用，而且已经有人告诉我，除非我增加供应，否则这样或那样的工厂将不得不减少运营，或者这样或那样的船只将无法航行。

此外，竞争性煤炭的库存已达到我们有记录以来的最低点，例外情况是1938年的四个月，当时由于当地敌对行动，总体局势无论如何都很特殊。

正如我在另一封信中所说，我相信许多人在他们的堆场里有煤炭储备，但当这些储备用完后，我不知道如何补充，除非在不久的将来采取一些措施来改善局势。

这是我在新年第一天为您描绘的一幅黯淡图景。我希望我被证明是错误的。

此致，

L. Handley-Terry

J.T. Nash 先生，
工部局，
上海。

Police report, January 5, 1940

Coal Situation.

The coal situation prevailing in Shanghai at the end of December, 1939 does not appear to be very favourable, although the imports of bituminous coal are considerably higher than they were during November. It is not very likely, however, that imports will continue to improve, as there are various factors governing this phase of the situation that must be taken into consideration.

It is learned that a large quantity of Fushun coal, which previously had been exported to Japan, is now being used by large industrial concerns and railways in Manchukuo. The resultant shortage of imports into Japan will probably be made up from coal which previously had been entering Shanghai. As factories are gradually resuming operations in Japanese occupied areas under Japanese control, it is very probable that less coal from Japanese controlled mines will be available in the Shanghai open market in the future.

At one time, when the local dollar depreciated in value, it was thought that factories in Shanghai would considerably reduce the scope of their operations owing to the high price of raw materials. Now, however, owing to the almost total suspension of export trade from Central Europe, Shanghai factories are obtaining increased business. There is therefore the possibility that factory owners will find themselves in an awkward position, with an increasing coal consumption and a decreasing supply available. As it is probable that most factories have stocks of coal in hand, a shortage should not be felt in the immediate future, but reports all seem to support the view that there will eventually be a shortage of coal in Shanghai. There is not much possibility of North China mines being able to relieve the shortage as they are at present hardly able to meet the demands made upon them.

Stocks of anthracite coal are still available for household use, but prices will no doubt be considerably higher than they have been recently.

煤炭形势。

1939年底上海的煤炭形势似乎不太乐观，尽管烟煤的进口量比11月份有显著增加。然而，进口情况继续改善的可能性不大，因为必须考虑到影响这一阶段局势的各种因素。

据悉，此前出口到日本的大量抚顺煤，现在正被满洲国的大型工业企业和铁路所使用。由此造成的日本进口短缺，可能会由此前运往上海的煤炭来弥补。随着工厂在日本控制下的占领区逐渐恢复运营，未来上海公开市场上来自日本控制矿区的煤炭供应量很可能会减少。

此前，当本地银元贬值时，人们曾认为上海工厂会因原材料价格高昂而大幅缩减经营规模。然而现在，由于来自中欧的出口贸易几乎完全停滞，上海工厂的业务量反而有所增加。因此，工厂主们可能会发现自己陷入困境：煤炭消耗量增加，而可用供应量却在减少。鉴于大多数工厂可能手头存有煤炭库存，近期应该不会感到短缺，但所有报告似乎都支持这样一种观点，即上海最终将出现煤炭短缺。华北各煤矿缓解这种短缺的可能性不大，因为它们目前几乎无法满足对其提出的需求。

无烟煤库存仍可供家庭使用，但价格无疑会比近期 considerably 高出许多。

Police Report, December 4, 1939.

Coal Situation.

With regard to the coal situation prevailing in Shanghai
at the end of November, many of the remarks in the report of
October still hold good. The future position of the local market
still remains very uncertain and local dealers are reluctant to
express opinions which may eventually prove incorrect and mis-
leading.

One important feature, however, is the decrease in imports
of bituminous coal to Shanghai during the month under review.

Imports during September totalled approximately 140,000
tons, for October, 98,000 tons, whilst the figure for November
is as low as 50,000 tons. In explanation of this fact, it is
learned that, while stocks of coal are actually available in
Shantung, Japan and Formosa, it is becoming increasingly difficult
to transport stocks. The exports from these sources are under
the control of Japanese interests, who are compelled to charter
only Japanese ships for transport. As there is a very heavy
demand on Japanese shipping, it is thought probable that imports
in the near future may register a further drop. There does not
appear to be any possibility of Indian coal being imported for
some time to come, as with the exchange being so unfavourable,
it is impossible to offer Indian coal at competitive prices.

Another point worthy of mention is that the Shanghai
Power Company have chartered an extra four or five ships and,
instead of obtaining coal as before, on a "Delivered Shanghai"
basis, will in future transport their own coal direct.

Messrs. Hongay Coal Sales, Ltd. continue to hold optimistic
views for the future and state that they are experiencing no
trouble in obtaining stocks of anthracite. Freight charges,
however, continue to remain a big problem and it is possible that
any further increase in freights will result in prices of coal
being increased correspondingly.

警务报告，1939年12月4日。

煤炭情况。

关于11月底上海 prevailing 的煤炭情况，10月份报告中的许多评论仍然适用。本地市场的未来形势仍然非常不确定，本地商号不愿发表可能最终被证明是错误和误导性的意见。

然而，一个重要特点是，在审查期间，运往上海的烟煤进口量有所下降。

9月份的进口总量约为140,000吨，10月份为98,000吨，而11月份的数字低至50,000吨。为解释这一事实，获悉虽然山东、日本和台湾实际上有煤炭库存，但运输库存变得越来越困难。这些来源的出口受日本利益集团控制，他们被迫只租用日本船只进行运输。由于对日本航运的需求非常大，人们认为近期内进口量可能会进一步下降。在可预见的将来，似乎不可能进口印度煤炭，因为汇率如此不利，无法以具有竞争力的价格提供印度煤炭。

另一点值得一提的是，上海电力公司（Shanghai Power Company）额外租用了四五艘船，今后将直接运输自己的煤炭，而不是像以前那样在“送达上海”的基础上获取煤炭。

恒义煤号有限公司（Messrs. Hongay Coal Sales, Ltd.）继续对未来持乐观态度，并表示他们在获取无烟煤库存方面没有遇到任何困难。然而，运费仍然是一个大问题，任何运费的进一步增加都可能导致煤炭价格相应上涨。

Subject. Coal Situation.

Made by. D.P.S. Killingbeck Forwarded by. D.I. Crawford

With regard to the coal situation prevailing
in Shanghai at the end of November, many of the
remarks in the report of October still hold good.
The future position of the local market still remains
very uncertain and local dealers are reluctant to
express opinions which may eventually prove incorrect
and misleading.

One important feature, however, is the
decrease in imports of bituminous coal to Shanghai
during the month under review.

Imports during September totalled approximately
140,000 tons; for October, 98,000 tons; whilst the
figure for November is as low as 50,000 tons. In
explanation of this fact, it is learned that, while
stocks of coal are actually available in Shantung,
Japan and Formosa, it is becoming increasingly
difficult to transport stocks. The exports from
these sources are under the control of Japanese
interests, who are compelled to charter only Japanese
ships for transport. As there is a very heavy
demand on Japanese shipping, it is thought probable
that imports in the near future may register a further
drop. There does not appear to be any possibility
of Indian coal being imported for some time to come,
as with the exchange being so unfavourable, it is
impossible to offer Indian coal at competitive prices.

Another point worthy of mention is that the
Shanghai Power Company have chartered an extra

E.T. Nash, Esq.,
Secretariat,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.

Dear Mr. Nash,

With regard to your letter F. 30/12 of 7th November, it is extremely difficult to make any worthwhile observations as to the future coal position in this market. There are so many unknown factors which have an important bearing on the arrival of coal in this port, anyone of which, if guessed wrongly, can upset the general position considerably.

You ask me for my observations on the October Police Report.

The first paragraph is, I think, quite sound, and is in fact my own view of the situation.

Although the views expressed by the Hongay Sales and ourselves, as set forth in the second and third paragraphs of the report, appear contradictory, I do not think that they are necessarily incorrect.

From the point of view of Hongay Sales, who are operating almost entirely in a foreign currency, prices will fluctuate in accordance with exchange. They did moreover increase prices in September or early October to allow for the increase in freight rates which occurred at the outbreak of war in Europe and also for the depreciation in exchange. More recently their prices have dropped a little with the improvement of the dollar to 5d and more.

As far as we are concerned there has been no change in K.M.A. prices since 1st August and therefore some time we will have to make up for the very much higher cost of transporting coal from Chinwangtao to Shanghai.

It follows therefore that our two firms are looking at the picture from rather different angles.

As regards paragraph 4, I have referred already to the increase in shipping freight rates. The only point to note here is that it is hardly correct to say that rates averaged 3/ to 3/6d per ton during July to September; 4/-, 4/6, 5/-, per ton was much nearer the mark.

The last paragraph I should say was entirely correct.

You will note that I have skipped the question of whether there will be a shortage or not. In my own private opinion I feel that there may well be, and I give you a resumé of my reasons for so saying:-

If you would refer to a note I made for Sir Robert a short time ago, you will see that this market is dependent on ourselves, Japan, Tsingtao and India for its coal supplies. As far as I can see, Japan and Shantung are producing what was expected from them, but, as you will see from the Imports Table attached to the police report, nothing arrived from India, in October, except for the Power Company. With the present uncertainty over exchange, I think practically nothing
