pages.en:
CHINA PRESS.
NOV 6 1938

Coal Supply
In Shanghai
Said Adequate

600,000 Tons Expected
To Be Used Monthly
During Winter

Although Shanghai does not have an abundant stock of coal, it will not face a shortage of the fuel in the coming five cold months, it was learned from reliable sources.

While many are showing renewed interest in the local coal situation, in view of the advent of cold weather, THE CHINA PRESS learned that an ample stock of coal is available in Shanghai and more is coming from abroad. In other words, the situation is not so acute as many may think.

The present stock of coal stored in Shanghai was placed at more than 100,000 tons by an official of a well-known mining company. For the month of November, at least 150,000 tons are expected to arrive here from North China, Australia, Africa, and India.

The above figures apply only to bituminous or soft coal, but the situation of anthracite or hard coal will not be tense either, since there are at least 50,000 tons in store now. About 80,000 tons more of hard coal are expected here for this month, it was said.

600,000 Tons Burned

THE CHINA PRESS was informed that for the five cold months—between November and March—Shanghai consumes about 600,000 tons of coal, and about this amount will be imported here. The coal comes from the following sources:

The Kailan Mining Administration, whose yearly output is 5 to 6 million tons, will supply Shanghai with 350,000 tons. Imported coal from abroad for the next five months will total to 150,000 tons. The Nee Tai Shing and Company, Ltd., believed to be the biggest Chinese coal dealer in Shanghai, has lately imported 80,000 tons, while other local dealers will have an aggregate stock of 250,000. This would make a sum total of 803,000 tons of coal available for the winter, which will cover the quantity to be consumed here.

No Coal Shortage

“No, I do not see any possibility or probability that Shanghai will face a shortage in coal for this winter,” the informant said. Questioned why so many Chinese householders complain of their inability to buy soft coal at a reasonable price, he continued:

“That is due to the fact that local Chinese coal dealers are spreading wild rumors of the impending shortage in coal. This resulted in a hike of coal prices on the local market.”

Apart from that, another reason why the prices of soft and hard coal made such a steep increase was because of the reduced output of coal mines located in North China, Shansi and Honan, it was stated. As a consequence, Shanghai is compelled to import the fuel from abroad. The depreciated Chinese currency and freight expenses are responsible for the increase, too.

2,000,000 Tons Consumed

It was learned that the best quality of hard coal is selling at $48 per ton, while soft coal is selling at $42, freight included.

Normally, Shanghai burns about 2,000,000 tons of coal, but this year, due to the increase in population and concentration of factories here, as much as 3,500,000 tons are needed, THE CHINA PRESS was informed.

Of the latter figure, the Shanghai Power Company, which consumes the largest quantity of coal in Shanghai, requires about 500,000 tons.

The informant was of the opinion that it was possible to reopen the mines located in the Japanese-occupied areas in the interior, especially in Honan and Shansi. But this will take place some months later, he added.
pages.zh:
《大美晚报》。
1938年11月6日

据称上海
煤炭供应
充足

冬季每月
预计消耗
60万吨

虽然上海的煤炭储备并不丰富，但从可靠消息来源获悉，在接下来的五个寒冷月份里，上海不会面临燃料短缺。

尽管随着寒冷天气的到来，许多人对本地煤炭状况重新表现出关注，但《大美晚报》获悉，上海有充足的煤炭库存，且更多煤炭正从国外运来。换句话说，情况并不像许多人想象的那样严峻。

一家知名矿业公司的一位官员表示，上海目前的煤炭库存超过10万吨。预计11月份至少有15万吨煤炭将从华北、澳大利亚、非洲和印度运抵此处。

上述数据仅适用于烟煤或软煤，但无烟煤或硬煤的情况也不会紧张，因为目前至少有5万吨库存。据说，本月还将有约8万吨硬煤运抵此处。

燃烧60万吨

《大美晚报》获悉，在11月至3月这五个寒冷月份期间，上海消耗约60万吨煤炭，届时也将进口大致相同数量的煤炭。煤炭来源如下：

开滦矿务局年产量为500万至600万吨，将向上海供应35万吨。未来五个月从国外进口的煤炭总量将达到15万吨。尼泰盛有限公司（Nee Tai Shing and Company, Ltd.）被认为是上海最大的中国煤商，最近进口了8万吨，而其他本地经销商的总库存为25万吨。这将使冬季可用的煤炭总量达到80.3万吨，足以覆盖此地的消耗量。

无煤炭短缺

“不，我看不到上海今年冬天面临煤炭短缺的任何可能性或概率，”消息人士说。当被问及为何如此多的中国家庭抱怨无法以合理价格买到软煤时，他继续说道：

“这是由于本地中国煤商散布即将出现煤炭短缺的谣言所致。这导致本地市场煤炭价格上涨。”

除此之外，软煤和硬煤价格大幅上涨的另一个原因是位于华北、山西和河南的煤矿产量减少。因此，上海被迫从国外进口燃料。中国货币贬值和运费也是导致价格上涨的原因。

消耗200万吨

据悉，最优质的硬煤售价为每吨48美元，而软煤售价为每吨42美元（含运费）。

《大美晚报》获悉，正常情况下，上海每年燃烧约200万吨煤炭，但今年由于人口增加和工厂在此集中，需要多达350万吨。

在后一个数字中，上海电力公司作为上海最大的煤炭消耗户，需要约50万吨。

消息人士认为，重新开放内地日军占领区的煤矿是可能的，特别是在河南和山西。但他补充说，这将在几个月后发生。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES,
NOV 4 1938
Ample Supply
Of Coal Said
On Hand Here
Shipments For November
Also Heavy; 60,000
Tons From India
LARGE QUANTITIES OF
HARD COAL COMING
With the advent of the first
cold weather in Shanghai con-
siderable interest has been
expressed as to the available
coal supply in the city. It
was learnt yesterday that there
is an ample supply of coal here
to meet all present demands
and large shipments are on the
way.
More than 100,000 tons of soft coal
have been landed at Shanghai and
are under storage, while it is ex-
pected that the shipments for
November will be in the neighbour-
hood of 150,000 tons. The situation
with regard to hard coal is some-
what similar, it being stated that
there is a reserve supply of 50,000
tons here at the present time. Ship-
ments of hard coal for November
will reach an estimated 80,000 tons.
Excluding Power Company
The above figures exclude sup-
plies landed or ordered by the
Shanghai Power Company, which
consumes more fuel than any other
plant in Shanghai.
The manner in which the hostili-
ties changed the coal situation in
Shanghai is indicated by the fact
that about 60,000 tons of soft coal
will be shipped here from Calcutta
in November alone. Prior to the
trouble, Shanghai depended mainly
upon fields in China for her supply
of soft coal and the necessity for
going farther afield has naturally
raised prices very considerably.
Cost Of Importation
One dealer interviewed here yes-
terday estimated that it cost over
$40 a ton to land soft coal in Shang-
hai. The actual purchase price in
terms of the depreciated Chinese
currency was said to be $34.70,
while duty and landing costs ac-
counted for another $6. It was
stated that Calcutta coal is now re-
tailing in Shanghai for around $42
a ton.
The best quality of hard coal is
now selling at $48 per ton and at
$45 for smaller lump of the same
quality. In addition, the coal bri-
quette industry is assuming very
large proportions in Shanghai with
about 26,000 tons of this type of
fuel being produced each month.
Before the outbreak of the hostili-
ties only about 10,000 tons were sold
each month, the increase being due
to the growth in population and
the higher prices being asked for
fuel of a better grade.
（批：R
Lile
C 4/11）
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，
1938年11月4日
据称本地
煤炭供应
充足
11月 shipments 也
很繁重；6万吨
来自印度
大量
硬煤运抵

随着上海迎来首次寒冷天气，人们对城市可用煤炭供应表示了极大关注。昨日获悉，这里有充足的煤炭供应以满足所有当前需求，且大量货物正在途中。

超过10万吨软煤已卸在上海并入库储存，预计11月份的运量将在15万吨左右。硬煤的情况 somewhat similar，据称目前有5万吨的储备供应。预计11月份硬煤运量将达到8万吨。

不包括电力公司
上述数字不包括上海电力公司卸货或订购的供应品，该公司消耗的燃料比上海任何其他工厂都多。

战事改变上海煤炭状况的方式体现在这样一个事实：仅11月份就有约6万吨软煤将从加尔各答运抵此处。在麻烦发生之前，上海主要依赖中国的煤田供应软煤，而不得不从更远的地方获取自然大大推高了价格。

进口成本
昨日在此采访的一位经销商估计，在上海卸下软煤的成本超过每吨40美元。据说按贬值的中国货币计算的实际购买价格为34.70美元，而关税和卸货费用另占6美元。据说，加尔各答煤炭目前在上海的零售价约为每吨42美元。

最优质的硬煤现在售价为每吨48美元，同品质的小块煤售价为45美元。此外，上海的煤球行业规模变得非常大，每月生产约2.6万吨此类燃料。
在战事爆发前，每月仅销售约1万吨，增长是由于人口增长以及对更好等级燃料索要更高价格所致。
（批注：R
Lile
C 4/11）

CHINA PRESS.

OCT 8 1938

Coal Prices Not Expected
To Show Marked Increase

Shanghai Believed Not Facing Coal Shortage
As Large Quantities Are Being Imported
From Australia And India

Although a large number of local households has begun, in view of the fast approach of cold weather to stock up coal for future household use. Shanghai will not face a shortage in coal, THE CHINA PRESS learned yesterday.

Nor will the coal prices in local markets register a marked increase as time passes on.

According to an officer of the Shanghai Municipal Council, several coal importers in Shanghai are importing large quantities of coal from Australia and particularly India for local consumption.

This newly-imported coal, if sold at $46 per ton as it probably will be, will yield a profit of not more than 10 per cent to the importers, THE CHINA PRESS was informed.

Profiteering Denied

Current reports stating that many local coal merchants are making exorbitant increases in coal prices and thereby gain huge profits are refuted by the S.M.C. officer as well as an agent of a well-known mining administration.

Although it is true that the local price of household coal has increased to some $40 and $50 per ton as compared with last year's price of $20, the increase is only natural in view of the depreciation of Chinese currency and the foreign sources of the coal.

3,000,000 Tons

In normal times Shanghai consumes more than three million tons of coal, but now because of the suspension of operation of various factories caused by the war, the amount of coal consumed is only some two million tons.

Again, while formerly all the required amount of coal could be produced by Chinese and foreign mines located in China, this is found impossible due to the disruption of communications.

Of the 2,000,000 tons of coal to be consumed in Shanghai, well over half must be obtained from abroad, it is learned. Importing coal from abroad raises the prices due to freight. This, combined with the low Chinese exchange rates, naturally increases the prices of coal in Shanghai and anywhere else in China.

Reopening Of Coal Fields

It was suggested that the Shanghai Municipal Council, through consular channels, urge the reopening of certain coal fields in the interior in order that Shanghai may enjoy the normal supply. Several of these coal fields are located in Japanese-occupied areas.

This plan, according to the coal agent interviewed, would seem inadvisable for the time being, due to the present unsettled political and industrial conditions here.

DJ Henderson 4/2
C 5/10
8/10
pages.zh:
《大美晚报》。

1938年10月8日

预计煤炭价格
不会出现显著上涨

据信上海不会面临煤炭短缺
因正从澳大利亚和印度
进口大量煤炭

尽管鉴于寒冷天气迅速临近，许多本地家庭已开始储备煤炭以备将来家用，但《大美晚报》昨日获悉，上海不会面临煤炭短缺。

随着时间的推移，本地市场的煤炭价格也不会出现显著上涨。

据上海公共租界工部局的一位官员称，上海的几家煤炭进口商正从澳大利亚，特别是印度，进口大量煤炭供本地消费。

《大美晚报》获悉，如果这批新进口的煤炭以可能的46美元每吨的价格出售，进口商的利润将不超过10%。

否认牟取暴利

工部局官员以及一家知名矿务局的代理人驳斥了当前关于许多本地煤商大幅提高煤炭价格从而获取巨额利润的报道。

虽然家庭用煤的本地价格确实从去年每吨20美元上涨到了约40至50美元，但鉴于中国货币贬值和煤炭来源为国外，这种上涨是自然的。

300万吨

在正常时期，上海消耗超过300万吨煤炭，但现在由于战争导致各种工厂停工，煤炭消耗量仅为约200万吨。

此外，虽然以前所需的所有煤炭都可以由中国境内中外煤矿生产，但由于交通中断，这已被证明是不可能的。

据悉，在上海要消耗的200万吨煤炭中，超过一半必须从国外获得。从国外进口煤炭因运费而推高价格。加上中国汇率低迷，自然导致上海及中国其他地方的煤炭价格上涨。

重开煤田

有人建议，上海公共租界工部局通过领事渠道，敦促重开内地某些煤田，以便上海能享受正常供应。其中几个煤田位于日军占领区。

据受访的煤炭代理人称，由于目前此地政治和工业状况不稳定，该计划目前看来不可取。

DJ Henderson 4/2
C 5/10
8/10

pages.en:
SHANGHAI TIMES
OCT 5 1938

Coal “Price Famine” Is
Expected; Local Buyers
Becoming More Anxious

Very Serious Situation Is Envisaged In Shanghai
During Coming Months; Reliable Survey Might
Suggest Solution; Normal Supply Cut Off

SKYROCKETING PRICES BRING COSTS AS
HIGH AS 300% ABOVE NORMAL

The present indications are that unless something drastic is done to remedy the present situation with regard to coal, an insufferable state of affairs will exist here during the coming winter.

During the past few weeks individuals wishing to purchase coal, in both large and small quantities, have found that prices are so high that they present an almost appalling picture of what heating costs will amount to in the next six months.

Although an examination of list prices, as issued by a number of dealers in Shanghai, would seem to indicate that coal prices are at least within reason, the experiences of actual purchasers, taken as a whole, seem to present another side of the picture. In discussing the matter with local purchasers a representative of "The Shanghai Times" has been informed that the price of coal to-day is often 300 per cent. more than what it was two or three years ago.

The question is one which so universally affects all residents of the city that the suggestion has been put forth that some sort of an investigation into the matter, should be made by the Shanghai Municipal Council in the public interest. Those who have studied the situation closely for several months state that it is difficult to ascertain in what quarters profiteering is occurring, but that an official investigation might throw some light on this subject.

“High Price” Famine

Another point which has caused considerable interest is that which concerns the manner in which increased freight rates and the unfavourable rate of exchange have affected the price of coal in Shanghai. In other words, in informed quarters it is believed that there is some excuse for the increase in the price of coal, but that some dealers here have overstepped reasonable limitations in the matter.

It is also felt that in view of the very real seriousness of the situation that the Shanghai Municipal Council might be in a position, through Consular channels, to urge the reopening of certain coal fields in the interior so that Shanghai would be able to get its normal supply. In this connection it is pointed out that Shanghai is actually facing a coal famine despite the fact that large quantities of the more expensive grades are being brought in.

Some stress is laid on the fact that there has been some confusion with regard to this aspect of the situation, for although there may be no real lack of coal in Shanghai this winter, it will be virtually impossible to obtain any at a price that is not almost beyond reason, unless something is done in the very near future.

Solution Suggested

To cite an example of current coal prices, one large purchaser stated here yesterday that he is now paying $50 a ton for coal that he could get for $15.50 per ton three years ago.

It is quite possible that some landlords will have to cut down on the number of hours during which they can provide heat, and it will be noted that this system has already been applied to the supply of hot water in a number of apartments. The burden will most naturally fall most heavily upon those who live in the older type dwellings and can least afford to cope with the increasing cost of heating.

The conclusion which is generally reached by those who are close to the trend of events, and fully realize the seriousness of the prospects for the coming winter, is that the time is ripe for some sort of unbiased survey which might possibly suggest a solution or, at least, assist the public in making a fair appraisal of the situation which it must face.
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》
1938年10月5日

预计煤炭将出现“价格饥荒”；本地买家日益焦虑

预计未来几个月上海局势将十分严峻；可靠的调查或许能提出解决方案；正常供应已中断

价格飞涨，成本高达正常水平的300%

目前的迹象表明，除非采取 drastic（严厉/彻底）措施来改善当前的煤炭状况，否则在这个即将到来的冬季，这里将出现令人难以忍受的局面。

在过去几周里，无论是大量还是少量购买煤炭的个人都发现，价格高得惊人，几乎让人对接下来六个月的取暖费用感到恐惧。

虽然查看上海一些经销商发布的标价单似乎表明煤炭价格至少还在合理范围内，但实际购买者的整体经历似乎呈现出另一番景象。《上海泰晤士报》的一位代表在与本地购买者讨论此事时获悉，如今的煤炭价格往往比两三年前高出300%。

这个问题普遍影响到本市所有居民，因此有人建议，为了公共利益，上海公共租界工部局应对此事进行某种形式的调查。那些密切研究这一局势数月的人表示，很难确定暴利行为发生在哪些环节，但官方调查可能会使这一问题真相大白。

“高价”饥荒

另一个引起极大关注的问题是，运费上涨和不利的汇率如何影响了上海的煤炭价格。换句话说，在知情人士看来，煤炭价格上涨有一定理由，但这里的一些经销商在此事上已经超出了合理的限度。

人们还认为，鉴于局势确实非常严重，上海公共租界工部局或许能够通过领事渠道，敦促重新开放内地某些煤矿，以便上海能够获得其正常供应。在这方面，有人指出，尽管有大量更昂贵的煤炭品种被运入，但上海实际上正面临煤炭饥荒。

有人强调，在这一方面存在某种混乱，因为虽然今年冬天上海可能并不真正缺乏煤炭，但除非在不久的将来采取某些措施，否则 virtually（实际上）不可能以并非几乎高得离谱的价格买到任何煤炭。

建议解决方案

为了举例说明当前的煤炭价格，一位大型购买者昨天在这里表示，他现在每吨煤炭支付50美元，而三年前他只需每吨15.50美元就能买到。

完全有可能，一些房东将不得不减少提供暖气的时间，值得注意的是，这种制度已经应用于许多公寓的热水供应。负担最重的自然将是那些居住在老式住宅中、最无力应对日益增加的取暖费用的人。

那些密切关注事态发展并充分认识到即将到来的冬季前景严重性的人普遍得出的结论是，现在时机成熟，可以进行某种公正的调查，这或许能提出解决方案，或者至少帮助公众对其必须面对的局势做出公平评估。

Coal Dealers :

ber 29, "Coal Dealers Fined in

煤炭经销商：

Shortage

暗示煤炭短缺

开滦矿业产量较此前减少50%。

Coal Shortage In
Near Future Said
Threatening Here

According to Chinese reports
from Japanese sources, the problem of
coal supply has become serious in
Shanghai. The major reason given
is that the mines of the Kailan
Mining Administration, which sup-
plied bituminous coal in large
quantities in previous years, are
producing 50 per cent less at present
due to labor troubles earlier this
year. The administration, the re-
port continues, is making efforts to
increase the supply of coal to
Shanghai.
It is also stated that Chinese
firms are seeking to bring a large
quantity of charcoal from the inter-
ior to this port. Stocks are re-
ported to be sufficient to meet local

pages.zh:
1447

称近期煤炭短缺威胁上海

据来自日方消息源的中文报道，上海的煤炭供应问题已变得严重。给出的主要原因是，往年大量供应烟煤的开滦矿务局的矿井，由于今年早些时候的劳资纠纷，目前产量减少了50%。报道继续称，该局正在努力增加对上海的煤炭供应。

报道还指出，中国公司正试图将大量木炭从内地运至本港。然而，据报道目前的库存足以满足本地需求。报道最后指出，关于储存在浦东的煤炭，70%已被运至黄浦江此岸。

pages.en:
Predicted Coal
Shortage Felt

Evepost Report Proved
Correct; Profiteers
Now Active

Vindication! Truth will out!
Slightly over a month ago, the
coal situation in Shanghai came
up for close scrutiny in a feature
article printed by the Shanghai
Evening Post and Mercury on
November 2. This story definitely
made out a case for an unliked
but nevertheless true coal short-
age.
For its pains, the Evepost re-
ceived a few tons of bricks the
next morning as contemporaries
had gone to the trouble to check
up on the c..l situation and then
came out with qualified state-
ments that as there were ample
stores on hand and shipments
were expected in the near future,
Shanghailanders had no cause to
worry about their cold bones when
the North Wind came into his
own around these parts.
Letter to Editor
Yesterday morning, (going step
by step in the giving of evidence
for the defense of the Evepost),
a contemporary printed a letter
from a correspondent. This re-
called previous announcements
that there were "thousands of tons
of coal, both anthracite and
bituminous, available in Shang-
hai for distribution throughout the
winter months." This announce-
ment was definitely reassuring,
but, on studying the situation to-
day, one is forced to the conclu-
sion that either this statement
was totally incorrect or there has
developed another price racket."
The latter continues in asking the
authorities to curb the present
high prices for the coal available.
The contemporary that printed
this letter yesterday also printed
an editorial on coal profiteering,
and a passage in this editorial
reads, "A correspondent in an-
other column raised the question
of coal prices in Shanghai at the
moment, and in doing so refers
to earlier statements to the effect
that there were sufficient supplies
of coal in Shanghai to last well
through the winter. That state-
ment was to some extent discount-
ed in well informed quarters,
though even then there was suf-
ficient indication to show that
Shanghai was not unreasonably
short." The editorial also sug-
gests that proper action be taken
against the profiteering it says
is possibly going on.
Shortage Denied
However, on November 3, our
contemporary printed this morning
after the Evepost's declaration of
coal shortage, story under a head-
line, "No Coal Shortage In
Shanghai", and this read, "Re-
ports of a coal shortage in
Shanghai yesterday morning were
denied by the S.M.C. authorities
when questioned on the subject
yesterday...During the past few
weeks the coal situation has de-
finitely improved...able to con-
cern itself by them (the public
utility companies) with regard to
a possible shortage of coal." The
story adds notes on supplies of
coal in Shanghai and forthcoming
shipments.
Another contemporary the same
morning printed the following,
"Despite reports to the contrary,
there is no need for anxiety re-
garding the coal supplies of the
city for the coming winter, accord-
ing to those who have made a
close study of the situation since
the outbreak of local hostilities
....Fears that there might have
been a shortage during the next
few months are regarded as
groundless." It further explains
and emphasizes supplies of King
Coal in Shanghai, and the ship-
ments expected.
Post Story
All these articles followed close-
ly on the Shanghai Evening Post
and Mercury's effort, which point-
ed out on November 2 that "The
present state of affairs indicates
that Shanghailanders are in for
a long, cold winter....It's simply
because there isn't a big enough
coal reserve....Reassuring state-
ments were made by the public
utility firms to the effect that
sufficient stocks are on hand, but
in general a coal shortage has been
actually felt by many individuals
....The problem of the coal supp-
ly is as great as that of food-
stuffs."
In conclusion, it may be point-
ed out that prices are very high
now, that Shanghailanders are
complaining of coal shortage and
that the situation is about as bad
as that of foodstuffs.—Despite the
fact that there were stores of coal
in Shanghai and the fact that
shipments were expected, and did
come in.
pages.zh:
感受到预测中的煤炭短缺

《晚邮报》报道被证实正确；牟利者现在活跃

平反！真相终将大白！

就在一个多月前，11月2日，《上海晚邮报与水星报》（Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury）在一篇特写文章中对上海的煤炭形势进行了仔细审查。这篇报道明确论证了一个不受欢迎但却真实的煤炭短缺案例。

作为回报，《晚邮报》第二天早上收到了一些砖头（意指批评或攻击），因为当时的其他报纸费心去核实煤炭情况，随后发表了一些保留态度的声明，称由于手头有充足的储备，且预计近期将有货物装运，当北风在这些地方肆虐时，上海居民无需担心他们的冷骨头。

致编辑的信

昨天早上（一步步为《晚邮报》的辩护提供证据），一家同行报纸刊登了一封读者来信。这让人回想起之前的公告，称上海有“数千吨无烟煤和烟煤可供整个冬季月份分配”。这一公告确实令人安心，但是，在研究今天的局势后，人们不得不得出结论，要么这一陈述完全错误，要么已经出现了另一种价格操纵集团。”

该信继续要求当局遏制现有可用煤炭的高价。

昨天刊登这封信的同行报纸还刊登了一篇关于煤炭牟取暴利的社论，其中一段写道：“另一位专栏的读者提出了当前上海煤炭价格的问题，并在这样做时引用了早期的声明，即上海的煤炭供应充足，足以顺利度过整个冬季。这一说法在消息灵通人士中在一定程度上打了折扣，尽管即使在那时也有足够的迹象表明，上海的短缺并非不合理。”社论还建议对其所说的可能正在发生的牟取暴利行为采取适当行动。

否认短缺

然而，在《晚邮报》宣布煤炭短缺后，我们的一家同行报纸在今天早上（11月3日）刊登了一篇标题为“上海没有煤炭短缺”的报道，文中写道：“昨天上午有关上海煤炭短缺的报道遭到上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）当局的否认，他们在昨天被问及此事时……在过去几周里，煤炭形势肯定有所改善……能够由他们（公用事业公司）关注可能的煤炭短缺问题。”该报道补充了关于上海煤炭供应和即将到货的情况说明。

同一天早上，另一家同行报纸刊登了以下内容：“尽管有相反的报道，但据那些自本地敌对行动爆发以来密切研究局势的人士称，没有必要对本市即将到来的冬季煤炭供应感到焦虑……对接下来几个月可能出现短缺的担忧被认为是毫无根据的。”它进一步解释并强调了上海“煤炭之王”的供应以及预期的装运量。

《晚邮报》的报道

所有这些文章都紧随《上海晚邮报与水星报》的努力之后，该报在11月2日指出，“目前的局势表明，上海居民将面临一个漫长而寒冷的冬季……这仅仅是因为没有足够大的煤炭储备……公用事业公司发表了令人安心的声明，称手头有充足的库存，但总体而言，许多人实际上感受到了煤炭短缺……煤炭供应问题与食品供应问题一样严重。”

总之，可以指出的是，现在价格非常高，上海居民抱怨煤炭短缺，局势与食品供应情况差不多一样糟糕。——尽管上海有煤炭库存，且预计并有货物实际运抵。

28714

Hoarding Principal Cause Of
High Prices In Shanghai

S. M. C. Finding Coal
Profiteers Hard
To Curb

By GEORGE LEONOF
Whenever a city passes through
a stage of conflict such as Shang-
hai has seen for four months, the
internal conditions of the town are
inadvertently unsettled. Many fac-
tors contribute to this unsettled
state of affairs, not the least of
which is profiteering and hoarding
by merchants and dealers, who dare
not sell their stock for fear of diffi-
culty of replacement.
So food prices have soared to a
new high during the hostilities,
and among other commodities, coal
has reached an unprecedented
"altitude."
But the fact that food and coal
are hard to obtain does not neces-
sarily mean that there is an im-
mediate shortage in this town. As

has already been pointed out, the
scarcity is due to the reluctance
of dealers to put their entire stock
on the market.
Control Food Prices
The Shanghai Municipal Council
has worked wonders with the food
problem. The city fathers have
evolved a plan whereby, by having
dealers depending upon them for
the transportation of food from the
Yangtse port, they are able to more
or less control prices. Further, be-
cause the S.M.C. gives merchants
protection against racketeers in the
food business, the prices have been
kept as low as possible.
Food prices are higher, but this
is unavoidable. The cost of bringing
food down from, say, Nantungchow
at the present high rate of trans-
portation can not be compared with
the transportation of food from
areas in the immediate vicinity of
Shanghai, as Pootung, for instance,
under normal conditions.
However, large stocks are still

Some Justification For
Increased Charges
For Food

available in Shanghai. To give an
example, fish is plentiful in local
cold storages. But judging from the
price of fish, one would get the im-
pression that fish in Shanghai is
about as plentiful as admirals in
Switzerland.
But these fish are the property
of individual concerns, who have no
wish to flood the market with their
sea-food, and supply a quantity
daily which just falls short of the
demand. Prices soar automatically.
Neither the S.M.C. nor any other
public body has control over the
companies, and short of com-
mandeering the stock, which is im-
possible, there is nothing that can
be done officially.
It is the same with coal. Com-
plaints have been many to the
effect that either there is an acute
shortage of coal in the city or as
this was officially denied, somebody
is piling up a fortune by hoarding
the fuel and selling it at exorbitant
prices.

Hoarders Responsible
The latter, unfortunately, is true.
Certain retail dealers are profiteer-
ing and derive entirely unreason-
able profits from the sale of coal.
Agents are aware of this, but noth-
ing can be done to solve the situa-
tion yet, as far as they are con-
cerned. The only logical solution
would be to flood the market with
coal and this, considering the pre-
sent transportation difficulties, is
hard to do.
Consignments of coal are arriv-
ing slowly but surely. However,
there is never more in the city than
just enough to supply the imme-
diate demand. One well-known local
agent told THE CHINA PRESS that
he wished no advertisement or pub-
licity whatsoever. He would not
even consider a free advertisement,
pointing out that he had just enough
coal to supply old and steady cus-
tomers, and that he had no wish
to be referred to by the general
public for his fuel.

28714

囤积是上海
物价高涨的主因

工部局发现难以
遏制煤炭奸商

乔治·列奥诺夫（GEORGE LEONOF）撰

每当一座城市经历像上海过去四个月所遭遇的那种冲突阶段时，其内部状况往往会不知不觉地陷入动荡。造成这种动荡局势的因素有很多，其中不容忽视的一点是商人和经销商的牟取暴利与囤积居奇，他们因担心存货难以补充而不敢出售库存。

因此，在敌对行动期间，食品价格飙升至新高，而在其他商品中，煤炭的价格也达到了前所未有的“高度”。

但是，食品和煤炭难以获得的事实，并不一定意味着本市立即出现短缺。正如已经指出的那样，稀缺是由于经销商不愿将其全部库存投放市场所致。

控制食品价格

上海公共租界工部局在解决食品问题方面创造了奇迹。市政当局制定了一项计划，通过让经销商依赖工部局从长江港口运输食品，从而能够或多或少地控制价格。此外，由于工部局为食品行业的商人提供保护，使其免受勒索者的侵害，因此价格一直保持在尽可能低的水平。

食品价格确实较高，但这是不可避免的。目前运输费率高昂，将食品从例如南通（Nantungchow）运下来的成本，无法与正常条件下从上海附近地区（例如浦东）运输食品的成本相提并论。

然而，上海仍有大量库存

一些增加食品
收费的理由

可供使用。举个例子，当地冷库中鱼类供应充足。但从鱼价来看，人们会得出一种印象，即上海的鱼就像瑞士的海军上将一样稀少。

但这些鱼属于个别商行所有，他们无意让海鲜充斥市场，每日供应量略低于需求量。价格便自动飙升。无论是工部局还是其他公共机构都无法控制这些公司，除非征用库存——而这又是不可能的——否则官方无能为力。

煤炭的情况也是如此。投诉很多，称要么市内煤炭严重短缺，要么正如官方否认的那样，有人通过囤积燃料并以过高价格出售来大发横财。

囤积者应负责任

不幸的是，后者属实。某些零售经销商正在牟取暴利，并从煤炭销售中获得完全不合理的利润。代理人对此心知肚明，但就他们而言，目前尚无任何措施可以解决这一局面。唯一合乎逻辑的解决方案是让煤炭充斥市场，但考虑到目前的运输困难，这很难做到。

煤炭货物正缓慢但确凿地抵达。然而，市内的存量从未超过仅够满足即时需求的数量。一位当地知名代理人告诉《字林西报》（THE CHINA PRESS），他不希望做任何广告或宣传。他甚至不考虑免费广告，指出他只有足够的煤炭供应给老主顾和固定客户，并且他不希望被公众视为其燃料的来源。

pages.en:
Effect Of "Squeeze" In
High Price Of Coal Here
Explained During Survey

Many Dealers Making As Much As $20 On One Ton
Of Coal In Shanghai; Hard Rocks Painted
Black Are Sometimes Sent In Orders

200,000 TONS OF COAL HELD ACROSS RIVER
WOULD RELIEVE SHORTAGE

A survey of the local coal situation made here yesterday by representatives of "The Shanghai Times" revealed the fact that the optimism which prevailed earlier in the season was quite unjustified. Those who have given the scale of prevailing retail prices and the manner of distribution to the small consumer careful consideration state that the average householder here is in a rather serious predicament.

It is admitted in official circles that it would be exceedingly hard to put a stop to the widespread profiteering which is going on among small coal dealers, but consumers who are confronted with flagrant cases are urged to get in touch with the committee in charge. It is recognized, on the other hand, that an increase in transportation charges and a big demand for coal elsewhere are among the many disturbing factors confronting the importers of coal to Shanghai.

In some circles the fact is deplored that more publicity has not been given to the quantity of coal lying in Pootung. It is estimated that there are about 200,000 tons of coal in this area, and, according to coal dealers here, the release of this would carry Shanghai through a period of unprecedented difficulty. Most of this coal is owned by Chinese companies, but it is most urgently hoped that some arrangement regarding its disposition may be reached in the near future.

Little Hard Coal

Interviewed here yesterday, one official who is well-informed on the situation stated that it is not generally realized that the public can buy its coal from the big dealers direct and in this way avoid paying the "squeeze" demanded by petty coal merchants. This condition applies to soft coal only, there being an insufficient supply of hard coal in Shanghai for the time being.

Certain petty dealers here have been buying soft coal in Shanghai for around $23 per ton and selling it a few hours later for $35, and in most instances the customer has been none the wiser. According to reliable information obtained here yesterday, lump coal is purchaseable at $23 per ton and dust coal at $20. Dealers in hard coal who were approached here yesterday for prices stated that they were unwilling to give them out.

The explanation for this was that any publicity given to reasonable prices now would cause such a rush on their offices that the police would have to be called in to keep order. It was explained that there are many people in Shanghai paying "squeeze" prices for coal who would jump at the chance to obtain the same quality at the usual market price.

This is not to say that all small dealers in Shanghai are dishonest, while local residents are doubtless familiar with any number of retail merchants who have not taken advantage of the situation. Any denial that there is a great deal of "squeeze" going on is, however, simply not to be reconciled with the true facts of the situation.

Rocks In Coal

One thing that has been brought to the attention of the better dealers is that not only are certain concerns putting their prices up sky-high, but they are also mixing good coal with that of an inferior quality and selling the product for all the market will bear. Not a few householders in Shanghai have been surprised to find that after their coal has been burnt in the furnace, large chunks of rock are to be found in the ashes. These are inserted to add weight and bulk to an order, and some dealers go so far as to paint the rocks black so that they will match the coal.

There is also little doubt in the minds of those who are familiar with the situation that the question of trucking has added materially to the high price of coal here, although there has naturally been an unpreventable increase in the price of transportation. It is hardly believable, however, that it costs any dealer $20 a ton to deliver coal from the wharves to his place of business. A more normal spread is that accepted by one large concern here, which states that customers can buy $23 coal for $19.65 at the wharf and $20 coal for $16.65.

Shipments Coming

It was ascertained here yesterday that large deliveries of hard coal are expected from Indo-China during the latter part of next month, one informant stating that 30,000 tons should be delivered in Shanghai between now and the first part of February. In the meantime dealers in hard coal are having a difficult time in even supplying their old customers and are turning down new orders every day.

They are occasionally working under a system whereby their oldest customers are being given a preferential price, but it is difficult to obtain information as to what this may be. Hard coal importers say that the shipping question is most complex, since the big firms in this line here do not own their boats and have to charter them for the trip from Indo-China.

A great many ships have been taken off the Shanghai-Hongay run because of the demand for transports for rice, while the better shipping rates in the United States and Europe have also been a contributory factor. It is also pointed out that all freight and duty charges must be paid in foreign currency.

Situation Summarized

Summarizing the situation as a whole, it has been suggested here in informed circles that a stronger official control should be exerted to minimize the practice of "squeeze" and that further representations should be made to the Japanese military authorities for the release of the coal stored in Pootung. It is also pointed out that the small householder should at least have the same advantages in purchasing coal on the market this winter as that enjoyed by the dealers and large purchasers, for, in its own way, this commodity is just as essential as food.
pages.zh:
调查期间解释
此处煤炭高价中
“盘剥”的影响

许多经销商在上海每吨煤炭上获利高达20美元；有时订单中会混入涂黑的硬石块

20万吨煤炭存于对岸
若释放可缓解短缺

《上海泰晤士报》（The Shanghai Times）的代表昨天对本地煤炭情况进行了调查，揭示了一个事实：本季早些时候流行的乐观情绪是毫无根据的。那些仔细研究了现行零售价格规模以及向小消费者分销方式的人表示，这里的普通住户正处于相当严重的困境中。

官方人士承认，要制止在小煤炭经销商中普遍存在的牟取暴利行为极其困难，但敦促面临公然案例的消费者与负责委员会联系。另一方面，人们也认识到，运输费用的增加以及其他地方对煤炭的巨大需求，是上海煤炭进口商面临的众多干扰因素中的两个。

在某些圈子里，人们对浦东（Pootung）积压的煤炭数量未得到更多宣传表示惋惜。据估计，该地区约有20万吨煤炭，据这里的煤炭经销商称，释放这批煤炭将使上海度过一段前所未有的困难时期。这些煤炭大多归中国公司所有，但人们迫切希望在不久的将来能就其处置达成某种安排。

块煤稀少

昨天在此接受采访的一位熟悉情况的官员表示，公众普遍没有意识到，他们可以直接从大经销商处购买煤炭，从而避免支付小煤炭商人要求的“盘剥”费用。这种情况仅适用于软煤，因为目前上海块煤（硬煤）供应不足。

这里的某些小经销商以每吨约23美元的价格在上海购买软煤，几小时后以35美元的价格售出，而在大多数情况下，顾客并未察觉。根据昨天在此获得的可靠消息，块煤可按每吨23美元购买，粉煤可按20美元购买。昨天在此询问价格的块煤经销商表示，他们不愿意透露价格。

对此的解释是，如果现在公布合理的价格，会导致他们的办事处遭到蜂拥抢购，以至于必须召警察来维持秩序。据解释，上海有许多人正在支付含“盘剥”的高价购买煤炭，如果有机会以通常的市场价格获得同等质量的煤炭，他们会欣然接受。

这并不是说上海所有的小经销商都不诚实，而当地居民无疑熟悉许多没有利用这一局势的零售商人。然而，任何否认存在大量“盘剥”行为的说法， simply 与实际情况的真实事实不符。

煤中掺石

引起较正直经销商注意的一件事是，某些商行不仅将价格抬得极高，还将优质煤与劣质煤混合，并以市场所能承受的最高价格出售该产品。上海不少住户惊讶地发现，煤炭在炉膛中燃烧后，灰烬中会出现大块岩石。这些岩石是为了增加订单的重量和体积而插入的，有些经销商甚至将岩石涂成黑色，以便与煤炭相匹配。

对于那些熟悉情况的人来说，毫无疑问，卡车运输问题也实质性地推高了这里的煤炭价格，尽管运输价格的上涨自然是不可避免的。然而，很难相信任何经销商将煤炭从码头运至其营业场所的成本会高达每吨20美元。更正常的价差是一家大型商行所接受的，该商行表示，顾客可以在码头以19.65美元购买原价23美元的煤炭，以16.65美元购买原价20美元的煤炭。

货物正在运抵

昨天在此获悉，预计下个月后期将有大量块煤从印度支那运抵，一位消息人士称，从现在到二月初，应有3万吨运抵上海。与此同时，块煤经销商甚至连供应老主顾都感到困难，每天都在拒绝新订单。

他们偶尔实行一种制度，给予最古老的客户优惠价格，但很难获得有关具体优惠幅度的信息。块煤进口商表示，航运问题最为复杂，因为这里的大型 firms 不拥有自己的船只，必须包租船只从印度支那航行。

由于对大米运输船的需求，许多船只已撤出上海-海防（Hongay）航线，而美国和欧洲更优惠的运费率也是一个促成因素。还有人指出，所有运费和关税必须以外国货币支付。

局势总结

综上所述，知情圈子建议，应加强官方管控，以最大限度地减少“盘剥”行为，并应向日本军事当局进一步交涉，要求释放储存在浦东的煤炭。还指出，今年冬天，小住户在购买市场煤炭时应至少享有与经销商和大买家相同的优势，因为就其自身而言，这种商品与食品一样必不可少。

pages.en:
COAL PROFITEERING
A correspondent in another column raises the
question of coal prices in Shanghai at the
moment, and in doing so refers to earlier state-
ments to the effect that there were sufficient
supplies of coal in Shanghai to last well through
the winter. That statement was to some extent
discounted in well informed quarters, though
even then there was sufficient indication to show
that Shanghai was not unreasonably short. The
present high prices undoubtedly suggest that
factors other than those which should ordinarily
dominate a market may be in operation, and it
is suggested that profiteering in coal is in pro-
gress. Judging from what has happened in con-
nection with other commodities there is little
reason to think that this suggestion is in any
way far-fetched. It is an undoubted fact that,
directly the state of emergency arose, certain
of the more unscrupulous elements in Shanghai
sought to make increased profits out of the
situation. People who owed their very safety
to the peculiar constitution of this city, and
were in fact guests within its borders sought to
satisfy their rapacity out of the pockets of those
whose very presence here protected them from
danger. In the case of rice the Municipal Coun-
cil has taken steps which have safeguarded the
interests of hundreds of thousands of Chinese in
the most effective manner. Undoubtedly there
are all manner of obstacles to prevent similar
action in all commodities, but coal is an essen-
tial, especially during winter. It does not seem
unreasonable, therefore, to suggest that an in-
quiry might be made into local coal stocks and
some method devised, if profiteering is found to
exist, of putting a stop to it. The argument that
that there is no provision for such things being
done may sound convincing enough in ordinary
circumstances, but as matters stand at the
present there are many who believe that action
should come first and discussion follow, if
necessary.
pages.zh:
煤炭牟取暴利

另一栏的一位通讯员提出了目前上海煤炭价格的问题，并在文中提及早前的声明，即上海的煤炭供应足以顺利度过整个冬季。这一说法在知情圈子里在一定程度上打了折扣，尽管即使在那时也有足够的迹象表明上海并没有不合理地短缺。目前的高价无疑表明，除了通常主导市场的因素外，可能还有其他因素在起作用，有人指出煤炭投机正在进行中。从其他商品发生的情况来看，几乎没有理由认为这一建议有任何牵强之处。毫无疑问，紧急状态一旦出现，上海某些更无良的分子便试图从局势中获取更多利润。那些依靠这座城市特殊的构成才得以保全性命、实际上是境内客居的人们，却试图从那些因其身处此地而免遭危险的人们的口袋中满足其贪婪。在稻米问题上，工部局采取了措施，以最有效的方式保障了数十万中国人的利益。毫无疑问，要在所有商品上采取类似行动存在各种障碍，但煤炭是必需品，尤其是在冬季。因此，建议对本地煤炭库存进行调查，如果发现存在牟取暴利行为，则 devise 某种方法予以制止，这似乎是合理的。那种声称没有规定允许采取此类行动的说法，在正常情况下听起来可能足够令人信服，但鉴于目前的事态，许多人认为应先采取行动，如有必要再进行讨论。

pages.en:
COAL PRICES
Is There Profiteering ?

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—In the earlier days of this
"schemozzle," I recollect coming
across an inspired statement to the
effect that there were thousands
of tons of Coal, both An-
thracite and Bituminous, available
in Shanghai for distribution through-
out the winter months. This annou-
cement was definitely re-assuring,
but, on studying the situation to-day,
one is forced to the conclusion that
either this statement was totally in-
correct or there has developed an-
other prize "racket."

It was not so many years ago that
kitchen coal was $13 a ton and I
think I am right in saying that it
was $17 last winter, whereas to-day
it is $23. A retailer in the West-
ern District is demanding $28 for
this same coal.

Furnace coal quite recently was
$12 a ton, whilst last year it was
obtainable at $16; to-day the same
quality is $30.

These examples suffice to show
that Shakespeare's condemnatory re-
marks might apply to this borough,
but if, as I surmise, "racketeers" are
responsible, I am sure that the au-
thorities are quite capable of com-
batting their activities. They have
ably done so as far as rice is con-
cerned and I feel it is incumbent
that the Council adopt some measure
to put a stop to this unwarrantable
profiteering on Coal.

FANNY ADAMS.

Shanghai, Dec. 9.
pages.zh:
煤价
是否存在牟取暴利？

致《字林西报》编辑

先生，——在这场“混乱”的初期，我记得曾看到一则据称来自权威渠道的消息，大意是上海有数千吨无烟煤和烟煤可供在整个冬季月份进行分配。这一公告确实令人安心，但审视今日之局势，人们不得不得出结论：要么该消息完全失实，要么是又出现了一种新的特权“ racket ”（非法勾当/垄断经营）。

就在几年前，家用煤的价格为每吨13美元，我想我没记错的话，去年冬天是17美元，而今天则是23美元。西区的一家零售商对同一种煤索价28美元。

炉用煤不久前还是每吨12美元，而去年则可以16美元买到；今天同等质量的煤价格为30美元。

这些例子足以表明，莎士比亚的谴责性言论或许适用于本租界，但如果如我所推测，“racketeers”（不法商贩）是罪魁祸首，我相信当局完全有能力打击他们的活动。他们在米价问题上已得力地采取了行动，因此我认为工部局有责任采取某些措施，制止这种对煤炭毫无道理的牟取暴利行为。

范妮·亚当斯 (FANNY ADAMS)

上海，12月9日。

REGISTRATION OF LOCAL COAL AND CHARCOAL MERCHANTS

The local Coal and Charcoal Consumption
Control Committee has issued a notice to the effect
that coal and charcoal merchants who have not yet
registered either with this Committee or the Coal
Merchants' Association or the Machine-Made Briquette
Merchants' Association must do so between November 1 and
3. The notice intimates that merchants failing to
register after the stipulated period will not be
allowed to buy or sell their wares.

THURSDAY
THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 10, 1936
8632
Acute Coal
Shortage Is
Facing City
21-12-36
200,000 Tons Now In
Shanghai Less Than
Month's Supply
TRANSPORTATION IS
DISRUPTED BY WAR
Price Jumps $3 Within
Week; Low Water Af-
fects Ship Carriers
An acute shortage of coal today
threatens Shanghai as a result of
the unsettled condition in North
China which disrupted rail trans-
portation and the low water which
upset shipment of the fuel by
steamers.
A survey made by a CHINA
PRESS reporter yesterday among
the city's leading dealers and
mining companies showed that the
total stock on hand is slightly over
200,000 tons, counting both an-
thracite and bituminous coal.
This amount is not enough to
last for a month if the city's com-
bined industrial and household
consumption continues at the rate
of 9,000 tons a day.
Utilities Not Affected
So far the dearth of supply has
not affected Shanghai's leading
public utility concerns—the power,
gas and water companies—whose
yearly requirements are contracted
by dealers.
However, the rising price, jump-
ing some $3 during the past week,
has dealt hardship to smaller fac-
tories, apartment house owners and
householders.
The ruling price quoted yester-
day by local dealers for first grade
Shansi anthracite was $20 per ton.
This price is some $3 or $4 higher
than the figure quoted last week.
The price of bituminous coal has
been boosted to $13 per ton, $4
higher than last week. While these
figures only include top grade fuel,
the same trend running between
$2, $3 and 4, is to be found in all
kinds of second and third grade
coal.
One of the two reasons which
brought about the shortage was the
dislocation of rail traffic in North
China as a result of the Suiyuan
fighting. Shansi mines which
furnish the local market with its
anthracite coal have not been able
to ship their output on the Cheng-
ting-Taiyuan Railway to Shihkia-
chwang, Hopei and thence along the
Peiping-Hankow Railway to Tangku
where the fuel is sent up to this
city by boats.
Shipments Reduced
Dealers also explain that they
have not been able to obtain freight
cars on the Tientsin-Pukow Railway
for transporting coal to Shanghai.
The Hua Tung Mining Company,
with their mines at Hsuchow, has
been forced to cut down its supply
to this part of the country from 30,-
000 tons a month to 15,000 tons a
month.
Another factor in this depleted
supply is the low water on the
chief rivers of China. Steamers
carrying coal of ...
has been forced to hold
1,500 tons ...

星期四
《大美晚报》，1936年12月10日，星期二
8632
城市面临
严峻的
煤荒
21-12-36
上海现存20万吨
不足一月之需
运输因战争
而中断
一周内价格上涨3美元；
水位低影响轮船运输

由于华北局势动荡导致铁路运输中断，加之水位偏低扰乱了蒸汽船燃料运输，上海今天面临着严峻的煤炭短缺危机。

《大美晚报》记者昨日对本市主要经销商和矿业公司进行的调查显示，包括无烟煤和烟煤在内的总库存量略高于20万吨。

如果本市工业和家庭综合消费量继续保持在每天9,000吨的水平，这一数量不足以维持一个月。

公用事业未受影响

截至目前，供应短缺尚未影响上海主要的公用事业机构——电力、煤气和水务公司，其年度需求已由经销商签订合同保障。

然而，过去一周上涨约3美元的价格，给小型工厂、公寓业主和家庭用户带来了困难。

本地经销商昨日报价的一级山西无烟煤价格为每吨20美元。这一价格比上周报价高出约3至4美元。

烟煤价格已涨至每吨13美元，比上周高出4美元。虽然这些数据仅包含顶级燃料，但在所有二三级煤炭中，也发现了2、3和4美元的相同涨幅趋势。

造成短缺的两个原因之一，是因绥远战事导致的华北铁路交通瘫痪。向本地市场供应无烟煤的山西煤矿，无法经正太铁路将其产品运至河北石家庄，再沿平汉铁路运至塘沽，然后通过船只将燃料运抵本市。

运输量减少

经销商还解释称，他们无法在津浦铁路上获得用于向上海运输煤炭的车皮。拥有徐州矿区的华东煤矿公司，被迫将其对该地区的供应量从每月30,000吨削减至每月15,000吨。

导致供应 depleted （枯竭）的另一个因素是中国主要河流的水位偏低。运载煤炭的轮船……

REPORT
Subject Cheap sale of coal briquettes - to be resumed
Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

D.L.
(Divisions)
Extra
Police not
necessary unless
unforeseen
difficulties
arise
R.D.C.
11/7

A seventh ten-day cheap sale of coal
briquettes will commence on July 11, 1940
and will be concluded on July 20.
Sales will begin daily at 2 p.m. and
continue until stocks are exhausted. Each
purchase will be limited to 5 catties or
30 cents worth of briquettes which is
equivalent to $120.00 per ton or $6 per tan.
A list of 50 distribution centres is
attached hereto.

C. Crawford
D. I.

D. C. (Special Branch)

Distribution
All D.U.s
All stations

R.D.C.
7月11日

第七次为期十天的煤球廉价出售将于1940年7月11日开始，至7月20日结束。
每日下午2时开始销售，直至存货售罄。每次购买限额为5斤或价值30角的煤球，相当于每吨120.00美元或每担6美元。
随函附上50个分销中心名单。

C. 克劳福德

JUN 1 4 1949

Cheap Coal-Balls
Available
Big crowds of poor are expected
to throng coal shops tomorrow as the
Shanghai Machine-made Coal Ball
Merchants' Association has again
decided to start another (and sixth)
cheap sale of coal balls. The quant-
ity of coal balls to be thus sold and
the shops where the cheap fuel
needed by the Chinese for cooking
will be sold, will be decided upon
at a meeting to be held this after-
noon. The price of coal balls is
following a downward trend, but it
is still beyond the reach of the poor.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
No. S. 1, Special Branch / Station / No
REPORT
Date May 17, 19 40.
File No. INDUSTRY
7555/S

Subject Coal Briquettes - Complain re high price of.

Made by. D.S.I. Hide Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford

With reference to the attached letters dated
May 8 and 9, from the "Residents in Yunnan Road"
and "Residents in Shantung Road" respectively,
requesting that the Council should order the
business associations to reduce the price of coal
briquettes, I beg to state that cheap sales of
coal briquettes are at present being conducted
under the sponsorship of the "Shanghai Municipality
Machine-made Coal Briquettes Factory Owners' Guild"
405 Tientsin Road, which has 49 distribution centres,
and the "Yi Tai Shing Coal Briquettes Factory",
380 Markham Road, which has 17 centres. Sales
are conducted both in the forenoon and afternoon
daily and prices range between approximately $6.70
and $8.00 per 100 "catties" or from $133 to $160
per ton, while the market price today is $8.40
per 100 "catties" or $170 per ton.

There appears no difficulty in obtaining
supplies at the designated centres though it is
true that even the reduced prices are more than
the average class Chinese can afford.

Since May 9, 1940, the principal Chinese coal
dealers have been quoting prices of coal dust
(from which briquettes are made) in U.S. dollars,
but are accepting Chinese currency at the prevailing
rate of exchange.

D. C. (Special Branch).
D. S. I.

关于附上的分别来自“云南路居民”和“山东路居民”的信件（日期分别为5月8日和9日），请求公董局命令同业公会降低煤球价格一事，谨此说明，目前煤球廉价销售是在“上海机制煤球厂业主公会”（天津路405号，设有49个分销中心）和“義泰興煤球厂”（马克姆路380号，设有17个中心）的主持下进行的。销售每日上午和下午均进行，价格约为每百斤6.70美元至8.00美元，即每吨133至160美元，而今日市场价格为每百斤8.40美元或每吨170美元。

15 MAY 1940
Translation of letter to Council
from "Residents in Shantung Road"
Dated 9th May, 1940.

Briquettes: High price of.

Since the 5th instant the local market has become
extremely tight. Food and fuel are the two principal daily
necessities. The price for briquettes, formerly fixed at $6
per picul, was already very high. During the last few days
the price of this article has suddenly jumped to $9.40. It is
stated that this unreasonable increase has not been approved
by the Price Control Committee and is largely due to the
manipulation of unscrupulous and hard-hearted profiteers
who unlawfully enrich themselves at the expense of the poor. The
increase in prices may also be attributed to the rumour-mongering
activities of certain individuals, whose object is to undermine
the local currency; such activities are more deadly than bombs
and guns. The authorities must give serious attention to this
matter. To save the four million war-afflicted residents in
this isolated city, the Council should also order the business
Associations concerned to reduce prices as soon as possible. We
shall be very grateful for such action.

(Signed) "Residents in Shantung Road".

(Note: Received for translation a.m. 14th May, 1940)

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 16 MAY 1940）
（印：模糊不清的椭圆形印章）

档案号 332/12
副本
1940年5月15日
致工部局信函的译文
发信人：“山东路居民”
日期：1940年5月9日。

煤球：价格高昂。

自本月5日以来，本地市场变得极度紧张。粮食和燃料是两项主要的日常必需品。煤球的价格此前定为每担6元，已经非常高昂。在过去几天里，该商品的价格突然跳涨至9.40元。据称，这一不合理的涨价并未得到物价管理委员会的批准，很大程度上是由于一些无良且黑心的投机商人的操纵，他们非法牟利，牺牲穷人的利益。价格上涨也可归因于某些人的造谣活动，其目的是破坏本地货币；这种活动的危害比炸弹和枪炮更致命。当局必须认真关注此事。为了拯救这座孤城中四百万受战争影响的居民，工部局还应命令相关的商业协会尽快降低价格。我们将对此举深表感激。

（签名）“山东路居民”。

（注：1940年5月14日上午收到以待翻译）

（印章：上海公共租界工部局总办处 1940年5月16日）
（印章：模糊不清的椭圆形印章）

Translation of letter to Council from
residents in Yunnan Road.
Dated 8th May 1940.

Briquettes: Serious rise in price

The situation in Shanghai has become worse since the 5th
instant. The price of briquettes has been increased from
$6.00 which is already very high, to $9.40 per picul without
the consent of the Price Controlling Committee. This unprecedented
situation is the result of unscrupulous manipulations on the part
of profiteers, unlawful and conscienceless. Beside profiteers
there are instigators whose object is to upset the Chinese
currency. The harm they are doing to the public is more
terrible than bombs and gunfire. Please instruct the Briquette
Dealers' Association to cut down prices at once.

(Signed)
Residents in Yunnan Road.

(Note: Received for translation a.m. 14th May, 1940).

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / TRANSLATION OFFICE）

1940年5月15日
供……用

致工部局信函的译文
发信人：云南路居民。
日期：1940年5月8日。

煤球：价格严重上涨

自本月5日以来，上海的局势变得更加恶化。煤球的价格已从原本已经很高的6.00元，未经物价管理委员会同意，上涨至每担9.40元。这种前所未有的情况是无良、违法且毫无良知的投机商人操纵的结果。除了投机商之外，还有煽动者，其目的是扰乱中国货币。他们对公众造成的危害比炸弹和枪炮更可怕。请指示煤球同业公会立即降低价格。

（签名）

Subject Resumption of Cheap Sale of Coal Briquettes, sponsored by the Shanghai Municipality Machine-made Coal Briquettes Factory Owners' Guild.
Made by. D.S.I. Hide Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford.

On the morning of May 13, 1940, the attached letter was received from the "Shanghai Municipality Machine-made Coal Briquettes Factory Owners' Guild", 405 Tientsin Road stating that at a meeting held by representatives of local briquettes factories, in the offices of the guild on May 11, 1940, the following resolution was passed :-

"That Cheap Sale of Coal Briquettes will be resumed between May 13 and May 31, 1940, at 49 distribution centres (29 of which are situated in the Settlement and the remainder in the French Concession). Sales will begin at 2 p.m. daily until the stock for the day is exhausted. Each purchase is limited to 6 catties for 40 cents." (approximately $133 per "ton")

The letter requests that police be detailed to maintain order at the distribution centres.
A list of 49 distribution centres is attached hereto together with translation.

1940年5月13日上午，收到来自位于天津路405号的“上海市机制煤球厂业主公会”的附函，信中称在1940年5月11日于该公会办公室举行的本地煤球厂代表会议上，通过了以下决议：-

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S S REGISTRY No. S. B. Dr. Stahoff Date May 13th 1940）
S. 1. Special Branch Station.
REPORT
Date May 13th 1940

Subject Coal Briquettes - situation.

Made by. D.S.I. Hide. Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford.

The following has been ascertained regarding the recent increases in the price of coal briquettes reported in the attached extract from the Shanghai Times and translation from the National Herold.

The 4th ten day cheap sale of coal briquettes sponsored by the Shanghai Municipality Machine-made Coal Briquette Factory Owners' Guild expired on May 5th 1940. For the purpose of discussing a 5th cheap sale period a meeting of Guild members was called for May 4th but failed to materialise owing to lack of support. It has been ascertained that guild members are desirious of maintaining a non-committal attitude regarding the resumption of cheap sales and fixture of prices as such has a tendency to limit their profits.

Prior to May 3rd, each increase in price was sanctioned by a meeting of guild members but increases since that date have not received such sanction.

On the morning of May 13th a letter was received from the guild announcing that a 5th cheap sale will commence on May 13th. It appears likely that the independent cheap sale conducted by the Nyi Tai Shing Coal Briquette Factory has forced the Guild into the resumption of cheap sales.

（印章：上海公共租界警务处 S S 登记处 编号 S. B. Dr. Stahoff 日期 1940年5月13日）
S. 1. 特务科分署。
报告
日期 1940年5月13日

主题：煤球 - 局势。

呈报人：副督察长 Hide。 转呈人：督察长 Crawford。

关于附件中摘自《字林西报》及译自《国家先驱报》的报道中提到的近期煤球价格上涨情况，已查明如下事实。

由上海市机制煤球厂业主公会赞助的第四次煤球廉价销售期于1940年5月5日结束。为了讨论第五次廉价销售期，原定于5月4日召开公会成员会议，但因缺乏支持而未果。经查明，公会成员希望就恢复廉价销售及固定价格问题保持不置可否的态度，因为这样做倾向于限制他们的利润。

在5月3日之前，每一次涨价都经过公会成员会议的批准，但此后的涨价未获此类批准。

5月13日上午，收到公会来信，宣布第五次廉价销售将于5月13日开始。看来，很可能是義泰興煤球厂独立进行的廉价销售迫使公会恢复了廉价销售。

May 4. 1940.
Morning Translation.

National Herald, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, Central China Daily
News, Circulation Daily News :-

MACHINE-MADE COAL BRIQUETTE TRADE GUILD TO MEET TO-DAY

Owing to the drop in the value of the
dollar., it was decided at a meeting which was
held by various briquette factories yesterday to increase
the sale price of briquettes from $7.40 to $8.50 per 100
catties or $23 per ton. This came into effect as from
yesterday.

According to one source of information,
the cause of the present increase in the cost price of
briquettes is due to shortage of supplies of coal dust
from the big coal mining companies.

On the other hand, it is reported that as
plentiful supplies of coal dust are arriving, local
residents hope that the authorities of the two Foreign
Settlements will adopt effective measures to stop unlawful
transactions in coal by the coal companies in order to
prevent speculators from attempting manipulation.

As it has not received any report about the
present increase in the sale price of briquettes, the
Machine-Made Coal Briquette Trade Guild is calling a joint
meeting of various factories at the Guild on Tientsin Road
at 2 p.m. to-day when it will perhaps stop the increase in the
price of briquettes.

1940年5月4日。
晨间译件。

《国民新闻》、《新晚报》、《申报》、《华中日报》、《循环日报》：-

机制煤球同业公会今日开会

由于美元贬值，各煤球厂昨日举行会议，决定将煤球售价从每百斤7.40元提高至8.50元，即每吨23元。该决定自昨日起生效。

据一消息来源称，目前煤球成本价格上涨的原因是大型煤矿公司的煤粉供应短缺。

另一方面，据报道，随着大量煤粉运抵，当地居民希望两租界当局采取有效措施，制止煤炭公司的非法交易，以防止投机商试图操纵市场。

由于尚未收到关于目前煤球售价上涨的任何报告，机制煤球同业公会将于今日下午2时在天津路公会召集各厂家举行联席会议，届时可能会停止煤球涨价。

May 10, 1940

Nyi Tai Shing Coal Briquettes Factory - Independent Cheap
Sale of Coal Briquettes
----------

With reference to the attached letter from
the Nyi Tai Shing Briquettes Factory, 380 Markham
Road, enquiries have ascertained that as from
May 11, 1940, the factory intends to conduct a
cheap sale of coal briquettes at 25 distribution
centres, 17 of which are situated in the Settlement
and the remainder in the French Concession.

A list of 17 centres in the Settlement is
attached hereto.

The first two centres (established for
the benefit of labourers) in the list will commence
the cheap sale daily at 9.30 a.m. until the allocated
supply is exhausted. Each purchase will be limited
to 15 catties for $1.20 (equivalent to approximately
$154 per ton). The remaining 15 centres
(established for the benefit of poor people) will
commence cheap sale daily from 2 p.m. until the
supply for the day is exhausted. Each purchase
will be limited to 5 catties for 40 cents
(equivalent to approximately $160 per ton).

This cheap sale by the Nyi Tai Shing Coal
Briquettes Factory will continue indefinitely.

All D.O.s.
All Stations    } Distributed p.m. 10-5-40

9 MAY 1940
PUBLIC WORKS

Translation of letter to Secretariat
from the Nyi T'a Hsing Briquette Factory.
Dated 7th May, 1940.

Briquettes: Cheap sales.

From 11th to 30th May we shall establish twenty centres
for the sale of briquettes to poor people. Each person will be
permitted to purchase 5 catties (Sz Ching) for 40 cents, and
40 piculs will be sold daily at each centre from 8 p.m. until
the allotted quantity is exhausted. Apart from the above,
five more centres will be established to sell briquettes to
labourers; each person to purchase 15 catties for $1.30, and
each centre to sell 60 piculs daily from 9.30 a.m. until the
supply is exhausted. A list of the addresses is enclosed
herewith. As we fear that ignorant persons may create
disturbance during the sales, will the Council please instruct
the various Police Stations concerned to detail one or two
Constables to each of the places mentioned to maintain order.
A similar letter has been addressed to the French Municipal
Council. Kindly favour with reply and grant our request.

(Signed and chopped)

Nyi T'a Hsing Briquette Factory
Yu Ts'eng-hsing
Address of Factory Office: 260 Markham Road.
Telephone: 39063.

Enclosure: 1 List.
(Note: Received for translation a.m. 8th May, 1940)

C. Aliano

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL / MAY 8 1940 / TRANSLATION OFFICE）

义泰兴煤球厂致秘书处的信函译文。

煤球：廉价销售。

从5月11日至30日，我们将设立二十个面向贫民销售煤球的中心。每人允许以40分购买5斤（市斤），每个中心每天从晚上8点开始销售40担，直至 allotted quantity（原文不清，意为分配数量）售罄。除上述外，还将设立另外五个中心向工人销售煤球；每人以1.30元购买15斤，每个中心每天从上午9:30开始销售60担，直至供应售罄。地址清单随函附上。鉴于我们担心无知之徒可能在销售期间制造骚乱，恳请工部局指令相关各警署派遣一至两名巡警到上述各地点维持秩序。已致函法国公董局提出同样请求。敬请回复并批准我们的请求。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 7555/8
Date 6/5/40
Morning Translation

Sin Wan Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, Shun Pao, Central
China Daily News:

FUEL SHOP OWNERS SEND LETTER TO S.M.C.

The Shanghai Coal Briquette and Firewood Shop
Owners' Guild yesterday sent the following letter to the
S.M.C. and the Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Commerce:-

We have received the following information
from various fuel retail shops:-
"On May 2 various large coal briquette
factories announced that all goods were sold out and
that the supply had ceased. Various retail shops are in
lack of coal briquettes to meet the demand of the public
and the Guild is asked to request the authorities for
relief."

Ordinarily, prior to a rise in the price of
goods, coal briquette factories supplied a certain quantity
of coal briquettes to various retail shops to meet the
demands of the public. Now taking advantage of the rise,
the factories have ceased sales and intend to create a
state of uneasiness, without any regard for the livelihood
of the people. The statement made by various factories
that the rise was due to the high cost of coal dust as a
result of the recent fall in the value of the Chinese
dollar is untrue.

It is learned that a certain factory produced
in ordinary days some 200 to 300 tons a day. This morning
an announcement was made to various retail shops that it
could only supply 20 tons of coal briquettes. It is
evident that this factory is contemplating hoarding supplies.
Coal briquettes are one of the daily necessaries
of life. We hereby request you to advise various coal
briquette factories to lower the price and to supply goods
as usual.

Sin Wan Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, Ta Mei Pao, Shun Pao
and Central China Daily News :-

In order to discuss matters relating to cheap
sale of coal briquettes, the Shanghai Machine-Made Coal
Briquette Trade Guild recently resolved to call a meeting
of representatives of various factories at 2 p.m. yesterday.
However, no meeting took place as none of the representatives
attended.

It is learned that the Guild in question will
probably not hold the fifth stage of the cheap sale of
coal briquettes.

According to information received, the Nyi
Tai Shing Coal Briquette Factory, with a view to rendering
relief to common people, will hold a cheap sale of coal
briquettes. The date and site where this sale will take
place may be announced to-day.

《新闻报》、《中美日报》、《申报》、《华中日报》：

燃料店主致信工部局

上海煤球柴片业公会昨日致信工部局及上海总商会，内容如下：-

吾等从各燃料零售店获悉以下信息：
“5月2日，各大煤球厂宣布货物售罄，供应停止。各零售店缺乏煤球以满足公众需求，故请公会请求当局救济。”

通常，在物价上涨之前，煤球厂会向各零售店供应一定数量的煤球，以满足公众需求。如今，各厂利用涨价之机，停止销售，意图制造恐慌状态，全然不顾民众生计。各厂声称涨价是由于近期中国货币贬值导致煤屑成本高昂，此说法不实。

据悉，某厂平日产量约为每日200至300吨。今早该厂向各零售店发布公告，称仅能供应20吨煤球。显然，该厂正图谋囤积居奇。煤球是日常生活必需品之一。吾等特此请求贵方劝告各煤球厂降低价格，并照常供货。

《新闻报》、《中美日报》、《大美晚报》、《申报》及《华中日报》：

为讨论煤球廉价销售相关事宜，上海机制煤球业公会近日决议于昨日下午2时召开各厂代表会议。然而，由于无代表出席，会议未能举行。

据悉，该公会可能不会举行第五阶段煤球廉价销售活动。

据收到的消息，义泰兴煤球厂为救济平民，将举行煤球廉价销售。销售日期和地点可能于今日公布。

12 APR 1940
POLICE FORCE

Translation of letter to Council from
Shanghai Chinese City Merchants' Briquette Committee.
S. S. REGISTRY
Dated 10th April, 1940. No. S. B. D. 7555/5
Date 14 / 4 / 40

Briquettes: Cheap sales and Police protection.

Beginning from 11th April the sale of briquettes at a
moderate price will continue for ten days, we yesterday
submitted a list of the addresses of various briquette shops
to the Council with the request that Police be sent to the
shops to preserve order. In the list the number of the Fuh
Hsing Company was wrongly given as 38, instead of No. 281,
Connaught Road; and the character 新 "hsing" was omitted
from the name of Zei Ts'ong Hsing, which is at No. 606
Macao Road, and not No 4201 Robison Road. As for the Zi
Zeng Chi establishment, Carter Road, it has been struck off
the list, while five shops, viz., the T'i Ta Wo establishment,
No. 254 Tatung Road, Kweng Wo Nyi Chi, No. 369 Yu Yuen Road,
Nyi Ziang T'a in Myburgh Road Market, Nyi T'a Haing Shop
Sales and Retail Department, No 380 Markham Road and Yuen
Fung Briquette Factory, No. 360, Lane 356 Jessfield Road, are
added in the list, thus making a total of 21 instead of 17
shops. Will the Council please notify the Police of the above
changes.

(Chopped) Wong Hsiao-lei
Chairman
Zi Chi-ch'ing
Member of Standing Committee

(Note: Received for translation a.m. 11th April, 1940)

（印：SHANGHAE MUNICIPAL COUNCIL）

S. S. 登记处
日期：1940年4月10日。编号 S. B. D. 7555/5
日期 40年4月14日

煤球：廉价销售及警方保护。

自4月11日起，将以适中价格继续销售煤球十天，我方昨日已向工部局提交各煤球店地址清单，并请派警察前往各店维持秩序。清单中福兴公司的门牌号误写为38号，应为康纳脱路281号；且位于澳门路606号（而非罗宾逊路4201号）的瑞昌新公司名称中漏写了“新”字。至于卡特路的资增记商号，已从清单中剔除，同时增加五家店铺，即：大通路254号的大和商号、愚园路369号的光华义记、缪尔赫路市场的严祥泰、麦根路380号的义泰兴商店批发零售部，以及极司菲尔路356弄360号的源丰煤球厂，从而使店铺总数由17家增至21家。请工部局将上述变更通知警方。

（盖章）黄孝雷
主席
资济清
常务委员

（注：1940年4月11日上午收到以待翻译）

（印：上海工部局）

10 APR 1940
POLICE FORCE

Translation of letter to Council from
Shanghai Chinese City Chamber of Commerce.
Dated 9th April, 1940.

Briquettes: Cheap sales

The second period for the cheap sale of briquettes ended
on 5th April. According to a resolution passed by briquette
dealers the sale at a moderate price will continue for 10 days
from 11th to 20th April. Each purchaser will be permitted to
buy daily 5½ catties (Sz ching, 斤市) for 30 cts. Of a total
of 30 shops which will conduct sales, 17 are in the Settlement
and 13 in the French Concession. A list of the names and
addresses of the shops is enclosed for the Council's information.
Please instruct the Police to maintain order at the shops during
the stated period and oblige,

(Chopped) Wong Hsiao-lei,
and Zi Chi-ch'ing.

Encl.: 1 list

(Note: Received for translation late a.m. 10th April, 1940).

及资济清。

30 MAR 1940
POLICE FORCE

Translation of letter to Council from
the Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Commerce.
Dated 28th March, 1940.

Briquettes: Cheap sale of: Police protection.
Seventeen shops in the International Settlement and
thirteen in the French Concession have been selected by the
Coal Dealers Association to sell briquettes at reduced price
from 27th March to 5th April. Each shop will retail to the
poor the fixed quantity of briquettes daily. As it is feared
that disturbances may result from the presence of large
crowds, a list of the shops is herewith enclosed and the
Council is begged to detail Police to the various establishments
during the above-mentioned period to maintain order.
(Chopped) Wong Hsiao-lai, Chairman
Li Chi-ch'ing, Member of Standing
Committee.

Enclosure: 1 list.

(Note: Received for translation, a.m. 29th March, 1940).

警务处

上海总商会致工部局信函译文。
日期：1940年3月28日。

煤球：减价出售：警方保护。
公共租界内十七家店铺及法租界内十三家店铺已由煤业公会选定，于3月27日至4月5日期间减价出售煤球。每家店铺每日向贫民零售固定数量的煤球。因担心人群聚集可能引发骚乱，现附上店铺名单，恳请工部局在上述期间向各店铺派遣警员以维持秩序。
（盖章）黄晓籁，主席
李济清，常务委员。

附件：清单1份。

（注：1940年3月29日上午收到以待翻译）。

REPORT
File No. 106
S.I. AL/...
No. S.B. D 614/77/S
Date March 21, 1940

Subject Shanghai Municipality Machine-made Coal Briquettes Factory
Owners' Guild - meeting

Made by D.S.I. Hide Forwarded by Supt. J. Mason

A meeting of representatives of local coal
briquettes factories was held in the offices of
the Shanghai Municipality Machine-made Coal Briquettes
Factory Owners' Guild, 405 Tientsin Road between
3.30 p.m. and 4.30 p.m. March 20, 1940. The
following resolutions were passed at the meeting
which was presided over by Mr. Zung Tsai Faung
( 陳萃芳 ), Chairman of the Shanghai Municipality
Machine-made Coal Briquettes Factory Owners' Guild:-

1) That a second ten day cheap sale of coal
briquettes be commenced on March 27, 1940
(five days after the present cheap sale
concludes on March 22nd.)

2) That a total of 1,000 tons of slack for
the manufacture of cheap sale briquettes
be supplied to smaller coal briquettes factories
by Nyi Tai Shing ( 義泰昌 ) Coal Co. (500 tons),
Dah Loong Shing ( 大隆興 ) Coal Co. (300 tons),
Tung Cheng ( 通成公司 ) Co. Ltd. (100 tons) and
Hargen & Co. ( 漢成公司 ) (100 tons) and that
distribution be made jointly by the guild
and the Chinese Chamber of Commerce.

3) That commencing from March 22, 1940, the wholesale
price of coal briquettes be raised from $110
to $120 per ton and the retail price from ¥5.80
to $6.40 per tan plus 20 cents transportation
fee. This decision is to be passed to the
Chinese Chamber of Commerce for sanction.

D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

报告

日期 1940年3月21日

事由 上海市机制煤球厂
业主公会 - 会议

由 副督察长 Hide 制作 经 警司 J. Mason 转呈

1940年3月20日下午3时30分至4时30分，本地煤球厂代表会议在天津市路405号上海市机制煤球厂业主公会办事处举行。会议由上海市机制煤球厂业主公会主席陈萃芳先生主持，会上通过了以下决议：-

1) 第二次为期十天的煤球廉价销售将于1940年3月27日开始（即在现行廉价销售于3月22日结束后的五天）。

2) 义泰昌煤号（500吨）、大隆興煤号（300吨）、通成有限公司（100吨）和漢成公司（100吨）应向小型煤球厂提供共计1,000吨用于制造廉价销售煤球的煤屑，并由该公会与上海总商会共同进行分配。

3) 自1940年3月22日起，煤球批发价格由每吨110元提高至120元，零售价格由每担5.80元提高至6.40元，另加20角运费。此决定将提交上海总商会批准。

Subject Kung Yung (公明) Coal Briquettes Factory

Made by D.S.I. Hide Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

Enquiries at the Shanghai Municipality
Machine-made Coal Briquettes Factory Owners' Guild,
405 Tientsin Road confirm the report in the Chinese
American Daily News of February 16th, 1940 that
the P.W.D. has ordered the Kung Yung Coal Briquettes
Factory, 699 Changping Road to close by March 8.
Removal was ordered in consequence of smoke
discharged from the factory in question, which
constitutes a nuisance to the neighbouring
residences. Following representation being filed
with the S.M.C. by the Chinese Chamber of Commerce
on behalf of the factory, the authorities concerned
have agreed to postpone the date of removal until
May 7, in order to allow the factory to find
a new site.
The Kung Yung Coal Briquettes Factory, which
has a daily capacity of 10 tons of briquettes, is
a member of the Coal Briquettes Factory Owners'
Guild, but has not been participating in the coal
briquettes cheap sale scheme sponsored by the guild.
Therefore, its removal or closure would not affect
the scheme.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
Translation of letter S B REGISTRY
Chinese number of No. S. B. D. 7558/2
Dated 24th February 1940.    3 / 140

Briquettes.

With regard to the advancement in the price of briquettes
this Chamber has on several occasions urged the machine-made
briquette dealers' association to instruct the various briquette
factories to increase their output to the maximum with the view
to forcing down the price. The coal dust used in the manufacture
of briquettes is obtained from mines in Anhwei. Each day the
Shanghai market requires 1,000 tons of dust, or 30,000 tons
per month; the dust is shipped to Shanghai via Haiphong. At
present the freight has been greatly increased; this also adds to
the cost of briquettes and to the difficulty of forcing the price
down. After repeated consultations with people in the briquette
business, it has been decided that the only way to solve the
question is to beg the Council to call a meeting of the responsible
persons of various steamship companies, and request them to lower
the freight so that briquette factories may increase their output
and sell at reduced prices. As this proposal, if carried out,
will tend to stabilize the livelihood of residents, the Council
is requested to give it support.

(Stamped) Wong Hsiao-lei, Chairman.
Tz Chi-ching, Member of Standing Committee.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 28 FEB. 1940）

(Note: Received for translation late a.m. 27th February, 1940).

煤球。

关于煤球价格上涨一事，本会曾多次敦促机器制煤球经销商协会指示各煤球厂最大限度地增加产量，以迫使价格下降。制造煤球所用的煤屑取自安徽的矿山。上海市场每天需要1,000吨煤屑，即每月30,000吨；煤屑经由海防运往上海。目前运费大幅增加；这也增加了煤球的成本以及压低价格的难度。经过与煤球业人士的反复磋商，决定解决此问题的唯一途径是恳请工部局召集各轮船公司负责人开会，请求他们降低运费，以便煤球厂可以增加产量并以降低的价格出售。由于此提议若得以实施，将有助于稳定居民生计，故请求工部局予以支持。

（盖章）王晓籁，主席。

URGENT

March 1, 1940.

Cheap Sale of Coal Briquette to be
conducted in the Settlement and
French Concession

The following resolutions were passed at
a meeting of the Coal Briquettes Cheap Sale Committee,
held at 4 p.m. 29-2-40, on the premises of the Chinese
Chamber of Commerce, 59 Hongkong Road, which was
presided over by Mr. Zee Chi Ching (徐寄庼),
executive of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce :-

1) That cheap sale of coal briquettes at $5.00
per "tan" be conducted between 2-3-40 and
21-3-40 at 26 designated centres in the
Settlement and French Concession. (List of
centres attached).

2) That each purchase be limited to 20 cents
worth (equivalent to 4 catties) of coal
briquettes only.

3) That cheap sale at these centres be commenced
at 2 p.m. daily until the stock allocated for
such purposes is exhausted.

Distribution
All D.O.s
All Stations
French Police

以下决议是在1940年2月29日下午4时于香港路59号中国商会会所举行的煤球廉价销售委员会会议上通过的，会议由中华总商会执行委员徐寄庼先生主持：-

1) 于1940年3月2日至3月21日期间，在公共租界和法租界的26个指定中心进行每担5.00元的煤球廉价销售。（中心名单附后）。

2) 每次购买仅限价值20分（相当于4斤）的煤球。

3) 这些中心的廉价销售每天下午2时开始，直到分配用于此目的的库存售罄为止。

上海市商會用箋

逕啓者本會為救濟界內居民燃料恐慌起見邀集煤球業同業公會
議決平賣煤球辦法計兩租界共設平賣地點二十六處期間暫定二
十天自三月二日起至三月二十一日止每日於下午二時起以廿六
廠售足其每日認售之數為止每人限售四市斤其價格為輔幣二角
該項平賣煤球廠在
貴局轄境者計十四處屆時誠恐人多擁擠相應函請
貴局隨時切警照料彈壓是為至企此致

26 FEB 1940
POLICE FORCE
FOR THE NECESSARY ACTION

Translation of despatch No.2095 from
the Shanghai Chinese City Chamber
of Commerce.

Dated 22nd February, 1940.

Briquette Factories: Police protection wanted.

Because the price of coal briquettes has advanced, the
residents in this city are greatly disturbed. Sometime ago the
machine-made "Briquettes Dealers' Association" called a meeting
of its members to devise measures for the cheap sale of coal
balls; it was then decided that the price of coal balls should
be fixed at $110.00 per ton or $5.80 per picul. An announcement
to the above effect was made by this Chamber and the Association.

There are twenty-four briquette factories which are members
of the Association; they are situated either in the Settlement
or the Concession. Since carrying out the decision for retailing
coal balls at low price within a specified period, the establish-
ments' premises have been overcrowded by customers. We now
beg to enclose herewith a list of the addresses of the factories.
Will the Council please instruct the Police Stations in the
mentioned localities to depute an adequate number of Constables
to the establishments to preserve peace and order and oblige.

(Chopped) Wong Hsiao-lei,
Chairman.

Encl.: List of Briquette factories.

(Note: Received for translation late a.m. Saturday, 24th Feb.1940).

上海中华市总商会第2095号公文译文。

日期 1940年2月22日。

煤球厂：请求警方保护。

由于煤球价格上涨，本市居民深感不安。前几日，机制“煤球同业公会”召集会员会议，商讨煤球廉价销售措施；当时决定将煤球价格定为每吨110.00元或每担5.80元。本商会与该公会已就此发布公告。

共有二十四家煤球厂为该公会会员；它们位于租界或法租界内。自执行在规定期限内零售低价煤球的决定以来，各机构场所内顾客拥挤不堪。现谨附上工厂地址清单一份。恳请公董局指令上述各地警察分局派遣足够数量的巡捕前往各机构维持治安秩序，不胜感激。

(盖章) Wong Hsiao-lei,
主席。

附件：煤球厂名单。

（注：1940年2月24日星期六上午晚些时候收到以待翻译）。

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / S.B. REGISTRY / No. S.B.D. 1156/40 / Date February 23, 1940）
S. 1. Special Branch
REPORT

Subject Shanghai Municipality Machine-made Coal Briquette Factory Owners'
Guild - meeting

Made by D.S.I. Hide Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

（批：D.C. / (Division) / R.W.Cf. / 22/2 / ）

Between 10 a.m. and 1 p.m. 22/2/40, a further
meeting of representatives of 18 coal briquettes
factories was held in the offices of the Shanghai
Municipality Machine-made Coal Briquettes Factory
Owners' Guild, 405 Tientsin Road. Mr. Nyien
Ngoeh Sung (嚴謬声), representative of the
Chinese Chamber of Commerce, was present during
the meeting which was presided over by Mr.
Zung Tsai Faung (張萃芳), Chairman of the Guild.
The following resolutions were passed.

1) That a letter be sent to each of the following
3 concerns requesting them to supply slack to
the coal briquette factories :-
1) Hargen & Co. C.
2) Tung Cheng Co. Ltd.
3) Dah Mow Co.

2) That an advertisement be inserted in the local
press by the Chinese Chamber of Commerce
informing the public that from date delivery
of coal briquettes will be made on payment
of extra 20 cents per "tan" in order to
reduce the inconvenience experienced by the
customers and the numbers congregated outside
retail shops.

3) That Mr. Zung Tsai Faung be detailed to
request Mr. Yu Ya Ching to negotiate with
shipping companies for a reduction of freight
charges on slack.

4) That the various public bodies consider
improvements in the cheap sale scheme.

5) That a letter be sent to the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce requesting that enquiries be made
regarding the production capacity of the coal
factories.

（批：Copies seen. C / （椭圆形印章，内容模糊） / C. 23/2. ）

D. S. I.

24 2/40 A.C. (Special Branch)

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / S.B. REGISTRY / No. S.B.D. 1156/40 / Date February 23, 1940）
S. 1. 特别班
报告

事由：上海市机制煤球厂业主公会——会议

呈报人：副督察长海德（Hide） 转呈人：督察长克劳福德（Crawford）

（批：D.C. / (Division) / R.W.Cf. / 22/2 / ）

1940年2月22日上午10时至下午1时，18家煤球厂的代表在天津市路405号上海市机制煤球厂业主公会办事处举行了进一步会议。华商总会代表严谬声先生出席了会议，会议由公会主席张萃芳先生主持。通过以下决议。

1) 致函下列三家商号，要求其向煤球厂供应碎煤：
1) 哈根公司（Hargen & Co. C.）
2) 同成有限公司（Tung Cheng Co. Ltd.）
3) 大茂公司（Dah Mow Co.）

2) 由华商总会在本地报刊刊登广告，告知公众自即日起，为减少顾客的不便及零售店外聚集的人群数量，交付煤球时每“担”需额外支付20分。

3) 委派张萃芳先生请求虞洽卿先生与轮船公司协商，降低碎煤的运费。

4) 各公共团体考虑改进廉价销售方案。

5) 致函华商总会，要求查询各煤球厂的生产能力。

（批：Copies seen. C / （椭圆形印章，内容模糊） / C. 23/2. ）

副督察长

1940年2月24日 A.C. (特别班)

Sir,

I beg to report that at about 7.a.m. on the 22/2/40, a telephone message was received from the "Kuo Hwa Coal Hong" (國華煤行), No.819 Sinza Road, to the effect that they were selling cheap coal briquettes and that a large crowd was gathering outside the said premises, and they required Police protection.

Questioned, the hong accountant stated that a notification had already been addressed to the Council acquainting them with the decision of the said hong to hold a sale of cheap coal briquettes.

Although no official notification had been received at the Station re the said sale, it was deemed advisable in the interests of peace and order to supply Police protection whilst the sale was in progress. Two C.P.Cs were accordingly detailed for such duty between 8 & 16.a.m and no untoward incident occurred.

From further enquiries it was ascertained that the aforementioned hong sold approximately 200 "tan" of cheap coal briquettes during the day.

The procedure adopted is as follows :-

A person wishing to make such a purchase visits the hong and is allowed to purchase one "tan" of briquettes at the cost of $5-80, on receipt of the money, the hong issue a voucher

On February 20th, 1940, Mr. Zung Tsai Faung
(陳萃芳), Chairman of the Shanghai Municipality
Machine-made Coal Briquette Factory Owners' Guild,
attended Police Headquarters and furnished the
following details relative to the coal briquette
situation.

On February 17th, a meeting of representatives
of the coal briquette factories was convened at the
Bankers' Club, 59 Hongkong Road, by Mr. Yu Ya
Ching who submitted a proposal that the wholesale
and retail price of coal briquettes be fixed at $110
per ton and $5.80 per "tan" respectively. This
proposition was adopted at a meeting of eighteen
representatives of coal briquette manufacturers
which was held at the Guild's premises at 405
Tientsin Road on the following day.

On February 20th the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce and the Shanghai Municipality Machine-made
Coal Briquette Factory Owners Guild published
a joint advertisement in the Chinese press announcing
the above decision and urging those concerned to
abide by it.

On the same day the guild addressed a letter
to the S.M.P. requesting assistance in the maintenance
of order should the necessity arise and enclosing
a list of member factories and sales offices, a
copy of which is attached.

February 20,1940.

To the Shanghai Municipal Police.

On the advice of the Chamber of Commerce,
member factories of this Association are selling

February 22, 1940.                                      Morning Translation

Chinese-American Daily News, Ta Mei Pao, National Herald, Sin
Wan Pao, Shun Pao, Central China Daily News :-

THE COAL BRIQUETTE PROBLEM

The Chinese Chamber of Commerce and the
Coal Briquette Factory Owners' Guild have laid down a
stipulation to the effect that the holders of godown
warrants must pay the godown charges and remove the coal
briquettes in the ten days between February 20 and 29,
failing which the delivery of goods will be stopped and the
goods will be taken back according to the original prices
and supplied to poor people. Holders of godown warrants
should pay careful attention to this matter.
Information secured by our reporter from
coal briquette merchants yesterday shows the following
quantities of coal briquettes held on godown warrants :-
1) Nyi Tai Shing (義泰興) Coal Briquette Factory - 5,500 tons
2) Kuo Hwa (國華) " " " 4,000 "
3) Nanyang (南洋) " " " 6,000 "
4) Tung Faung (東方) " " " 2,500 "
5) Yueh Tung (越東) " " " 500 "
6) Hu Lih Chen (胡立成) " " " 400 "
7) Pei Yang (北洋) " " " 250 "
8) Kwang Hwa (光華) " " " 600 "
9) Tsing Hwa (清華) " " " 300 "
10) Yuen Hwa (源華) " " " 200 "
11) Nan Faung (南方) " " " 500 "
12) Woo Kiang (吳江) " " " 600 "
13) Hwa Tung (華通) " " " 1,000 "

24 coal briquette factories, members of
the Machine-Made Coal Briquette Factory Owners' Guild, are
undertaking sale of coal briquettes at reduced prices.
However, when people approach fuel shops or coal briquette
shops for the purchase of coal briquettes, they cannot make
the purchases as the shop assistants reply that they have no
stocks. Demands above the supply available will be
experienced when people try to buy coal briquettes direct
from coal briquette factories.
It is learned that the interested quarters
are discussing measures to remedy the situation and to deal
with hoarders.

煤球问题

上海总商会与煤球厂业公会已制定规定，凡持有栈单者，必须在2月20日至29日的十天内支付栈租并提取煤球，否则将停止交货，并按原价收回货物，转而供应贫民。持有栈单者应密切关注此事。
本报记者昨日从煤球商处获悉，目前凭栈单持有的煤球数量如下：-

机制煤球厂业主公会的24家会员煤球厂正以降价方式销售煤球。然而，当人们前往燃料店或煤球店购买煤球时，却因店员答复无货而无法购买。当人们试图直接从煤球厂购买煤球时，将会出现供不应求的情况。
据悉，有关方面正在讨论补救局势及对付囤积者的措施。

pages.en:
上海市機製煤球業同業公會重要公告

查煤球為市民生活不可缺之燃料，近因市面波動，引起恐慌，經本會決議臨時救濟辦法如下：（一）自本月二十日起煤球售價每公噸一百五十元八角不得任意抬高。（二）煤球棧單持有人應於本月二十九日止十天之內繳付棧租出行發售期滿止現貨並另籌原價收回方法供應平民。（三）所有無棧車之柴炭店同業應請暫時忍痛在本月二十日起至二十九日止十天之內每日上午勿向煤球廠購煤球以便各廠將棧單交清下午再行發售。（四）請各煤球廠注意生產不使供給中斷以上四項辦法全為安定市況共濟時起見用特會同通告務希全市各煤球廠商柴炭同業及棧單持有人一體遵照辦理是所至盼。

May 6, 1940.
Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao :-

Hvi Tai Shing Factory to Hold Cheap Sale of Briquettes

Following the termination of the fourth cheap sale of coal briquettes, the Hvi Tai Shing Coal Briquette Factory has decided to hold a cheap sale of 2,500,000 catties of coal briquettes for the benefit of the public. The cheap sale will be held from May 11 to 30. 25 selling offices, of which five will look after the wants of labourers, will be established.

The following measures will be taken :-
1) 4,000 catties of coal briquettes a day will be sold by each selling office from 2 p.m. every day. Each person (not labourers) will be allowed to buy only 5 catties for 40 cents.
2) 6,000 catties of coal briquettes a day will be sold to labourers only from 9.30 a.m. every day. Each labourer will be allowed to buy 15 catties for $1.20.

The addresses of the selling offices will be announced on May 10.

《新闻报》、《申报》：-

惠泰兴厂将举行煤球廉价销售

继第四次煤球廉价销售结束后，惠泰兴煤球厂决定为公众利益举行250万斤煤球的廉价销售。廉价销售将于5月11日至30日举行。将设立25个销售点，其中五个将专门照顾劳工的需求。

May 6, 1940.
Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, National
Herald, Ta Mei Pao, Central China Daily News :-

AUTHORITIES SHOULD SUPPRESS UNLAWFUL INCREASE IN
PRICE OF COAL BRIQUETTES

The fourth cheap sale of coal briquettes held
by the Machine-Made Coal Briquette Trade Guild terminated
yesterday. More purchasers were seen yesterday, but most
of them failed to procure anything as all the briquettes
were sold out.
Due to the absence of the leading coal hongs
the meeting scheduled for yesterday has been postponed.
Five cheap sale places will be established by the Nyi Tai
Shing Coal Hong (義泰興), but due to the great demand
they are still insufficient. The production of coal
briquettes by the smaller factories has greatly decreased
for leading local coal hongs have not been able to obtain
sufficient coal dust. The stock of coal in Shanghai at
present is more than 100,000 tons and more than 6,000 tons
arrived on May 4. Reports of an alleged shortage of coal
dust are being spread by speculators for purposes of
profiteering.
The price of coal briquettes was increased
to $137 per ton on April 26, and to $160 on May 3.
When retail shops purchased coal briquettes from the
leading coal hongs yesterday, the price was further
increased to $178 per ton. During the past ten days,
the price has been increased on three occasions, the
increases totalling $41.
According to a certain coal and charcoal
shop owner, the retail shops were not informed in advance
of a price increase; when the former purchased coal
briquettes from leading coal hongs, an increased price
was quoted. A certain leading coal briquette hong usually
produced 100 tons a day, but it gives out that their daily
production is only 20 tons. Several retail shops have
to close their business as they have no stocks. Retail
shops have been blamed by the public for the increase in
the price of coal briquettes, but the price is controlled
by the leading coal hongs.
The Coal and Charcoal Trade Federation is
discussing measures to deal with hoarding and speculation
in coal briquettes.
